item.title: Ravens HC Jesse Minter said DT Nnamdi Madubuike (neck) will not play in Week 1 against the Colts.
item.description:
Nnamdi Madubuike BAL Defensive Lineman

Despite being a limited participant in practice all week, the Ravens will continue to exercise caution with Madubuike, who is attempting to return from what was once believed to be a career-ending neck injury. The 28-year-old lineman has had an encouraging offseason and training camp and could find himself on the field soon, but the Ravens will give him at least one more week to prepare. We’ll see if he’s able to suit up for Week 2 when the Ravens play host to the Saints.

Source: Baltimore Ravens

item.title: Zachariah Branch (hamstring) will play in Week 1 against the Steelers.
item.description:
Zachariah Branch ATL Wide Receiver

Branch was limited by the hamstring issue for the first two practices of the week. He got up to a full practice on Friday and was cleared for Week 1. Branch will likely see a few designed touches in his NFL debut, but fantasy managers will want to wait until he overtakes Olamide Zaccheaus on the depth chart before getting him into their lineups.

item.title: Falcons QB Cooper Rush will start in Week 1 against the Steelers.
item.description:
Cooper Rush ATL Quarterback

With two days left to go until the Falcons kick off the 2026 season, head coach Kevin Stefanski already finds himself on his third-string quarterback. With Tua Tagovailoa (oblique) and Michael Penix Jr. (knee) both banged up, Rush will draw the start on the road against the Steelers. This was already shaping up to be a tough matchup for the Falcons’ offense, but with Rush under center, it’s fair to say everybody in that offense will receive a slight downgrade as far as fantasy production is concerned. Rush completed 65.4 percent of his passes while throwing for 303 yards, no touchdowns, and four interceptions last year with the Ravens.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: Jonathon Brooks (groin) will play in Week 1 against the Bears.
item.description:
Jonathon Brooks CAR Running Back

Brooks missed time late in camp with “general soreness” that was later revealed to be a minor groin issue. He was limited in practice this week, but that seems like nothing more than maintenance for a player who has barely played football over the past two seasons. Dave Canales is understandably keeping his workload light, even in practice. Brooks is expected to split carries with Chuba Hubbard in Week 1. He will be a high-risk FLEX play before we know what his role looks like.

Source: Joe Person

item.title: Falcons QB Tua Tagovailoa (oblique) will not play in Week 1 against the Steelers.
item.description:
Tua Tagovailoa ATL Quarterback

The oblique injury Tua suffered on Thursday will be enough to sideline him for the season opener. Head coach Kevin Stefanski said Tagovailoa will be week-to-week with the injury, so his status will be one to monitor when next week’s injury report is released. An up-and-down offseason for the 28-year-old quarterback that started with a back injury and an underwhelming training camp has now snowballed into him missing Week 1 after he was handed the start in large because Michael Penix (knee) wasn’t deemed ready to go just yet. Given the circumstances that led to him being named the starter, it’s safe to say Tua was already on a short leash entering the season. If Penix is able to go in Week 2 against the Panthers, it’s possible Tua’s 2026 debut will be further delayed regardless of his health.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: Commanders EDGE Odafe Oweh (calf) will play in Week 1 against the Eagles.
item.description:
Odafe Oweh WAS Outside Linebacker

The Commanders will also have Daron Payne (knee) and K’Lavon Chaisson (knee) on the field for Sunday when they travel to Philly to take on the Eagles. Washington made several defensive additions this offseason in hopes of improving a unit that ranked among the league’s worst last season in its second year under Dan Quinn.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: Patriots placed WR A.J. Brown (ankle) on injured reserve.
item.description:
A.J. Brown NE Wide Receiver

This doesn’t come as much of a surprise after it was reported on Thursday that Brown could miss at least the next four games. Now that he finds himself on injured reserve, the star receiver won’t be able to return until at least Week 6 when the Patriots play host to the Jets. Brown caught just three passes for 26 yards in his debut with the Patriots before exiting the game. After running just four routes in the first half of Wednesday’s game, Mack Hollins ran 22 routes in the second half and should see an increase in snaps in the coming weeks. Brown’s absence should also pave the way for Romeo Doubs to see more looks in the passing game after he saw just three targets in Week 1.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: Jalen McMillan (knee) is doubtful for Week 1 against the Bengals.
item.description:
Jalen McMillan TB Wide Receiver

In addition to McMillan, the Buccaneers are also listing RB Sean Tucker (hamstring) as doubtful, putting both players on the wrong side of being active for Week 1. McMillan was able to log a limited week of practice, so hopefully he’ll have a chance to suit up in Week 2 when the Buccaneers take on the Browns. Rookie WR Ted Hurst should make for an interesting dart throw in DFS as he looks to be in line for more work with McMillan sidelined.

Source: Greg Auman

item.title: Bengals WR Emeka Egbuka (toe) will play in Week 1 against the Bengals.
item.description:
Emeka Egbuka TB Wide Receiver

Egbuka has been trending in the right direction all week after logging full practices on both Wednesday and Thursday. The second-year receiver gets a juicy Week 1 matchup against a Bengals team that was among the worst against the pass last season. While Cincinnati hopes some additions they’ve made on the defensive side of the ball should help turn things around this season, Egbuka will be a solid WR2 this week in what should be a high-scoring game.

Source: Greg Auman

item.title: Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) will play in Week 1 against the Eagles.
item.description:
Jacory Croskey-Merritt WAS Running Back

Croskey-Merritt was a limited participant in practice all week but is good to go for Sunday’s opener against the Eagles. “Bill” is expected to handle the majority of the backfield rush attempts on Sunday, but how he factors into the passing game will be worth monitoring. The second-year back has reportedly worked to improve in the passing game this year and could turn into a decent three-down contributor if the Commanders trust him enough in passing-down situations. Until we see how his usage unfolds, Croskey-Merritt shouldn’t be viewed as anything more than an RB3/FLEX option against the Eagles.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: Tua Tagovailoa (oblique) was not spotted at Friday’s practice.
item.description:
Tua Tagovailoa ATL Quarterback

Tua wasn’t spotted during the portion of practice open to the media, so it’s possible he takes the field later in the day. That said, his absence from practice on Friday wouldn’t bode well for his Week 1 availability after he popped up on Thursday’s injury report with an oblique issue. Veteran Cooper Rush took all first-team snaps for the Falcons on Thursday and would be in line to start on Sunday if Tua is unable to go. We should have an updated injury report soon, which will lay out Tagovailoa’s availability heading into the weekend.

Source: Marc Raimondi

item.title: Bengals CB DJ Turner (hamstring) will play in Week 1 against the Buccaneers.
item.description:
DJ Turner CIN Cornerback

Turner popped up on Thursday’s injury report with the hamstring issue, but head coach Zac Taylor said the fourth-year corner will be good to go for Sunday’s game. Turner posted career highs in pass breakups (18) and interceptions (2) last season while earning a PFF coverage grade of 78.1. The Bengals will rely heavily on him in Week 1 to slow down Baker Mayfield and a revamped Buccaneers passing game. While Turner is healthy and good to go, Taylor said DE Shemar Stewart (knee) is doubtful, making him unlikely to play in Week 1.

Source: Ben Baby

item.title: Tee Higgins (heel) will play in Week 1 against the Buccaneers.
item.description:
Tee Higgins CIN Wide Receiver

Bengals HC Zac Taylor said Higgins and fellow receiver Ja’Marr Chase (knee) will both be good to go for Sunday’s game against the Buccaneers. Higgins has been dealing with a heel/foot injury in recent weeks but will be on the field for the team’s season-opener. He profiles as a high-end WR2 in what is expected to be a high-scoring game to kick off the Bengals’ 2026 season.

Source: Ben Baby

item.title: Ja’Marr Chase (knee) will play in Week 1 against the Buccaneers.
item.description:
Ja'Marr Chase CIN Wide Receiver

Chase was a full participant in each of the Bengals’ first two practices to start the week and is good to go for Week 1, according to head coach Zac Taylor. Chase can be trusted as a high-end WR1 for fantasy players in a matchup against the Buccaneers that should be ripe for fantasy points.

Source: Ben Baby

item.title: Titans LB Cedric Gray (concussion) will not play in Week 1 against the Jets.
item.description:
Cedric Gray TEN Linebacker

Gray suffered a concussion over the weekend after being involved in an accident while driving an ultra-terrain vehicle. Gray is expected to be back on the field after he clears concussion protocol, but his absence creates a glaring hole in the middle of the Titans’ defense. Gray totaled 164 tackles and one sack last season. His absence could lead to an increased role for rookie Anthony Hill Jr. on Sunday.

Source: Turron Davenport

item.title: Jonathon Brooks (groin) was seen practicing on Friday.
item.description:
Jonathon Brooks CAR Running Back

We’ll have a better sense of Brooks’ Week 1 availability in a few hours when the Panthers release their final injury report for the week, but the third-year back logged limited practices on Wednesday and Thursday and is trending in the right direction for Sunday’s game against the Bears. If he’s active, Brooks is expected to split touches with Chuba Hubbard, which could put a hard cap on both players’ upside in the season-opener.

Source: Alex Zietlow

item.title: Jaguars HC Liam Coen said Parker Washington will “absolutely” be the team’s punt returner to start the season.
item.description:
Parker Washington

Coen also noted that Washington is “the guy right now,” suggesting that his role as the returner could change at some point in the year. Washington returned 25 punts for the Jaguars last season and racked up 341 return yards and two touchdowns on those returns. Coen said the Jaguars will hope to get Travis Hunter involved as the punt returner at some point, but Washington will start the season in the role. Washington profiles as a solid WR2 to start the fantasy season after going for 58-847-5 last year.

Source: Ryan O’Halloran

item.title: Commanders released OT D.J. Humphries.
item.description:
D.J. Humphries

Humphries’ release comes just a few weeks after the Commanders signed him to bolster an offensive line that had recently lost Laremy Tunsil. The veteran tackle apparently failed to make much of an impression in his brief stint with the Commanders, although it’s possible this is a roster management decision, and at some point he re-signs with Washington’s practice squad with a chance to be elevated in future weeks.

Source: Zach Selby

item.title: Patriots signed DT DaQuan Jones, formerly of the Bills, to a one-year contract.
item.description:
DaQuan Jones NE Defensive Tackle

According to NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport, Jones will receive $3.5 million in base salary with a chance to earn up to $6 million on his deal. The 34-year-old vet started in all 12 games he appeared in for the Bills last season, totaling 22 tackles, three TFLs, and three sacks while also forcing a fumble. Jones played under head coach Mike Vrabel from 2018 to 2020 and should provide immediate help up front for the Pats’ d-line.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: Jets CB D’Angelo Ponds (calf) is doubtful for Week 1 against the Titans.
item.description:
D'Angelo Ponds NYJ Cornerback

The Jets have not released their final injury report, but this news comes from head coach Aaron Glenn, who spoke with the media Friday morning. Ponds was a limited participant in each of the team’s first two practices this week, but the belief is he hasn’t had enough time to be ready for the season opener. It doesn’t sound like the second-round rookie has suffered any setbacks in his recovery, so hopefully he’ll be on track to make his debut in Week 2 against the Packers. Glenn also said RB Kene Nwangwu (back) is doubtful while EDGE Joseph Ossai (foot) and WR Tim Patrick (groin) will be held out of Sunday’s game.

Source: Rich Cimini

item.title: Jets HC Aaron Glenn said Jason Sanders will serve as the team’s kicker in Week 1 against the Titans.
item.description:
Jason Sanders NYJ Kicker

This is notable because Sanders is currently on the Jets’ practice squad while veteran kicker Blake Grupe is on the 53-man roster. Fantasy managers expecting Grupe to contribute to their Week 1 lineups will want to make sure they find a replacement. Sanders certainly makes for a viable option after he converted 37-of-41 field goal attempts last season while going 12-of-14 from distances of 50-plus yards.

Source: Rich Cimini

item.title: ESPN’s Josh Weinfuss reports “the expectation is that Jeremiyah Love will play Sunday against the Chargers.”
item.description:
Jeremiyah Love ARI Running Back

Weinfuss received this information from a source familiar with the situation, but this news isn’t all that surprising. Love has logged back-to-back limited practices to start the week, and ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported on Thursday that “it looks like” Love will suit up in Week 1. The first-round rookie is expected to split touches with Tyler Allgeier, who was listed as the RB1 on the Cardinals’ unofficial depth chart earlier this week, but we would still expect Love to see enough touches to warrant starting as a mid- to low-end RB2 in his regular-season debut.

Source: Josh Weinfuss

item.title: Cowboys signed Ryan Flournoy to a one-year, $6 million contract extension.
item.description:
Ryan Flournoy DAL Wide Receiver

Flournoy is now under contract through the 2027 season. The 26-year-old receiver caught 40 passes for 475 yards and four touchdowns last season, while finishing third among Cowboys receivers in routes run (273) and fourth on the team in targets. It was reported earlier this summer that he was seeing more snaps in the slot, but it’s hard to imagine Flournoy making enough of an impact to be fantasy-relevant as long as CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens, and Jake Ferguson are healthy.

Source: Jordan Schultz

item.title: Myles Garrett said his goal ahead of Week 2’s game against the Giants is to “get healthy.”
item.description:
Myles Garrett

Coming off an underwhelming debut in which he failed to even record a tackle in Week 1’s loss against the 49ers, Garrett said he was “the worst version” of himself in Thursday’s game. The star pass rusher was dealing with a knee injury in the days leading up to the game, but was ultimately removed from the injury report on Wednesday. Speaking after the game, he said his knee didn’t feel 100 percent, but Garrett still managed to play on 40 snaps, per PFF. Unfortunately, he generated only three pressures and failed to get a hit on the quarterback. Hopefully, some extended time off before next Monday’s game against the Giants will be enough for Garrett to get right in the Rams’ official 2026 home debut.

Source: Nate Atkins

item.title: 49ers HC Kyle Shanahan said Christian McCaffrey played through cramps in Week 1’s win over the Rams.
item.description:
Christian McCaffrey SF Running Back

McCaffrey’s usage was a bit underwhelming in the first half of Thursday’s win. The 30-year-old running back played on 20 offensive snaps to Kaelon Black’s, while Black’s seven rush attempts more than doubled the three carries we saw from CMC, who also saw six first-half targets. McCaffrey’s second-half usage saw a slight uptick, but it’s possible some of what we saw as it pertains to last night’s split was related to this cramping issue. McCaffrey was undoubtedly the more efficient of the two Niners backs in last night’s win, but Black was solid in his debut, rushing 14 times for 65 yards. McCaffrey should be positioned for a big Week 2 game next week against the Dolphins.

Source: Nick Wagoner

item.title: 49ers HC Kyle Shanahan said De’Zhaun Stribling’s Achilles was intact after Week 1’s win over the Rams.
item.description:
De'Zhaun Stribling SF Wide Receiver

Stribling was carted from the game late in the second quarter after briefly attempting to play through the ankle injury he suffered earlier in the game. While there was some concern that his injury was Achilles-related, Shanahan’s comments after the game suggest there’s little reason to be concerned about his Achilles at this time. Stribling played 21 snaps in the first half of Thursday’s game but was held without a catch. We’ll likely get more clarity on his status in the coming days, but hopefully the worst was avoided here.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: 49ers HC Kyle Shanahan told reporters that Jake Tonges suffered an MCL injury against the Rams.
item.description:
Jake Tonges SF Tight End

Shanahan told reporters that it “doesn’t look good.” The 27-year-old tight end suffered the injury near the end of the first half, and it sounds like San Francisco will be without the backup tight end for some time. Luke Ferrell will likely see more snaps with Tonges unavailable.

Source: Matt Lively

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: Tyler Higbee caught both of his targets for 12 yards in the Rams’ Week 1 loss to the 49ers.
item.description:
Tyler Higbee

Higbee ended up leading the Rams’ tight ends in targets and receptions, as Davis Allen had just one catch before exiting with a head injury, and Terrance Ferguson didn’t catch his only opportunity. Ferguson still seems like the tight end to roster going forward, but one could argue Higbee has the higher floor because he’ll see more snaps because of his blocking ability. That’s not a ringing endorsement, if it’s not obvious. The Rams will try and get it going against the Giants in Week 2.

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: Davante Adams caught 3-of-6 targets for 26 yards in the Rams’ Week 1 loss to the 49ers.
item.description:
Davante Adams

There was plenty of talk about how great Adams looked in the precursor to the season, but it wasn’t on display in Week 1. The 33-year-old had a long gain of just 13 yards, and he and Matthew Stafford were unable to find many openings against the San Francisco secondary. Adams will get a chance to rebound in Week 2 in a Monday Night Football contest against the Giants.

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: Puka Nacua caught 5-of-9 targets for 74 yards in the Rams’ Week 1 loss to the 49ers.
item.description:
Puka Nacua

Nacua did bring in a 41-yard connection in the first half, but outside of that, it was a disappointing first effort to the season for one of the best wideouts in the game. It’s tough to blame much — if any — of it on Nacua, as Matthew Stafford and the Rams’ passing attack were completely shut down by the 49ers’ defense. All things considered, it could have been worse. Nacua remains near the top of the wideout rankings for Week 2 against the Giants.

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: DeMarcus Robinson caught 2-of-3 targets for 50 yards and a touchdown in the 49ers’ Week 1 win over the Rams.
item.description:
Demarcus Robinson SF Wide Receiver

Robinson snagged one of three touchdown passes from Brock Purdy, with his being the longest connection on a 39-yard strike. The 31-year-old had just one other catch, and while he’s still capable of making a deep play or two, it’s hard to trust him as a fantasy option. He’ll have a chance to prove the doubters wrong again in Week 2 against the Dolphins.

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: George Kittle caught 2-of-5 targets for 12 yards in the 49ers’ Week 1 win over the Rams.
item.description:
George Kittle SF Tight End

Brock Purdy tried to get Kittle involved early in the contest, but it was the one legitimate option that Purdy wasn’t able to find success with. It’s amazing that the 32-year-old was even able to play in this game considering he tore his Achilles in January, but it is also fair to say it was a fantasy dud. Expect better things going forward for Kittle, and the next chance comes in Week 2 against a not-so-great Dolphins defense.

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: Deebo Samuel caught 6-of-7 targets for 48 yards and a touchdown in the 49ers’ Week 1 win over the Rams.
item.description:
Deebo Samuel SF Wide Receiver

In addition to those receptions, Samuel also added a rush for five yards and returned two kicks for 74 yards with a long of 45. The 30-year-old’s time with the Commanders was disappointing, but his return to San Francisco — at least in this first contest — was a successful one, even without much yardage. Samuel’s targets were likely helped by De’Zhaun Stribling leaving with an ankle injury, but the connection between Samuel and Purdy looked solid enough in the Australia opener. Samuel will be back in action in Week 2 in a matchup against the Dolphins.

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: Mike Evans caught 6-of-7 targets for 49 yards with a touchdown in the 49ers’ Week 1 win over the Rams.
item.description:
Mike Evans SF Wide Receiver

Evans made his debut with the 49ers and high-pointed a touchdown pass from Brock Purdy the way we’ve seen him do it for well over a decade with the Buccaneers. He did have a drop, but he was targeted early as the 49ers were pass-happy in the first half before needing less of an aerial attack over the final two quarters. Evans is always going to be a red-zone threat with his 6-foot-5 size, and stands a decent chance of scoring again in Week 2 against the Dolphins.

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: Blake Corum rushed 10 times for 54 yards in the Rams’ Week 1 loss to the 49ers.
item.description:
Blake Corum

Corum was unable to find the end zone while Kyren Williams did, but Corum was the more efficient tailback between the 20s with Williams only tallying 41 yards. He was also a non-factor in the passing game, but the Rams were basically a non-factor in the passing game with Matthew Stafford struggling to figure out the 49ers’ defense. Corum could see more touches in Week 2 against the Giants, but there’s no guarantee.

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: Kaelon Black rushed 14 times for 65 yards in the 49ers’ Week 1 win over the Rams.
item.description:
Kaelon Black SF Running Back

It was Black’s NFL debut, and all things considered, it was a pretty good one. The former Indiana star had four more carries than Christian McCaffrey and was much more involved in the rushing attack in the first half, though CMC was obviously a factor in the passing attack and Black had just one catch for five yards. It wasn’t the most impressive statline you’ll see from a debut, but there were definitely flashes that suggest success for the 24-year-old. Black and the 49ers will get a chance to face the Dolphins in Week 2.

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: Kyren Williams rushed 11 times for 41 yards with a touchdown in the Rams’ Week 1 loss to the 49ers while adding three catches for 24 yards.
item.description:
Kyren Williams

Williams’ day was salvaged with a short-yardage score. He finished with one more rushing attempt than Blake Corum, but Corum did look spryer with 54 yards on those attempts. The Rams’ offense just didn’t have it in the Australian showdown, and Williams should see a better box score in Week 2 against the Giants; even if Corum remains a fantasy adversary.

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: Christian McCaffrey rushed 10 times for 68 yards in the 49ers’ Week 1 win over the Rams, adding five catches for 20 yards.
item.description:
Christian McCaffrey SF Running Back

The man they call CMC was not a big part of the first-half attack, but saw plenty more touches over the final two quarters to turn what was looking like an ugly fantasy debut into a decent — although far from spectacular — outing for the 30-year-old veteran. It’s worth noting that Kaelon Black received 14 carries in the contest for 68 yards, and it’s likely that Black is going to be involved going forward in at least a somewhat similar capacity. McCaffrey should still get plenty of touches going forward, and should have a good day against the Dolphins in Week 2.

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: Matthew Stafford completed 15-of-25 passes for 155 yards with an interception in the Rams’ 27-7, Week 1 loss to the 49ers.
item.description:
Matthew Stafford

Stafford didn’t get much time to enjoy Australia, and likely won’t leave this contest with fond memories. He completed just 4-of-11 passes in the first half and didn’t do much better in the final 30 minutes, and outside of a 41-yard connection with Puka Nacua, he just couldn’t get the ball downfield. He was also stuffed on a fourth-and-goal run at the goal line to cement the poor day. Credit the 49ers’ defense, but it’s fair to call this a disappointing season debut for the reigning MVP. Expect a rebound in Week 2 against the Giants in a Monday Night Football contest.

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: Brock Purdy completed 25-of-34 passes for 205 yards with three touchdowns and one interception in the 49ers’ 27-7, Week 1 win over the Rams.
item.description:
Brock Purdy SF Quarterback

Purdy also added 29 yards on his five attempts. The veteran signal-caller did throw a terrible interception, but outside of that pick he played exceptionally well; even if most of his completions were for short yardage. All three passing scores came to different players, with his best throw being a perfectly placed touchdown to Deebo Samuel between two Rams’ defenders to cement the blowout. Purdy will look to keep it going in Week 2, and gets a friendly matchup against the Dolphins.

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: Davis Allen is being evaluated for a concussion.
item.description:
Davis Allen

Allen has one catch for 13 yards, and likely is done for the day. The 25-year-old backup will need to clear protocol to play in Week 2 against the Giants.

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: Jake Tonges (knee) has been ruled out for the remainder of Week 1 against the Rams.
item.description:
Jake Tonges SF Tight End

Tonges finished without a target before exiting near the end of the second quarter. The 27-year-old will have a chance to return in Week 2 against the Giants, but his status for that game — and the weeks after — should be updated by early next week.

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: Jake Tonges (knee) is questionable to return against the Rams in Week 1.
item.description:
Jake Tonges SF Tight End

Tonges limped off the field after suffering his knee injury near the end of the first half. Assuming he doesn’t return, Luke Ferrell will get the snaps behind George Kittle and feature in two tight end sets.

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: De’Zhaun Stribling (ankle) has been ruled for the remainder of Week 1 against the Rams.
item.description:
De'Zhaun Stribling SF Wide Receiver

Stribling was carted off during Friday’s contest, and finished without a catch in his NFL debut. He’ll get a little longer to potentially return for Week 2 against the Dolphins, but obviously his status for that contest is very much in doubt.

Source: San Francisco 49ers

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: De’Zhaun Stribling (ankle) exited Week 1 against the Rams on a cart.
item.description:
De'Zhaun Stribling SF Wide Receiver

Stribling hurt the ankle earlier in the contest, and while he was able to return shortly after, the rookie wideout was unable to continue and exited on the vehicle. It’s likely he won’t return to Friday’s game, but there should be an update on his status soon.

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: Cowboys signed TE Brevyn Spann-Ford to a three-year extension through 2029.
item.description:
Brevyn Spann-Ford DAL Tight End

Spann-Ford initially signed on with the Cowboys as a 2024 undrafted free agent. He has caught 18 passes for 178 yards and one touchdown since then. The front office is evidently pleased with his development. He is not worth rostering in 12-team leagues. The deal is worth $18 million with $12.075 million guaranteed.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: Cardinals EDGE Josh Sweat (knee/rest) was limited on Thursday.
item.description:
Josh Sweat ARI Outside Linebacker

Sweat barely practiced this summer, supposedly dealing with a knee injury, while the Cardinals brass assured reporters that there was nothing to see here. The player was reportedly displeased with the team, but as of Week 1 practices, he remains a Cardinal. He is on track to face the Chargers this weekend.

Source: Arizona Cardinals

item.title: Rams declared WR Tutu Atwell, WR CJ Daniels, OL Bill Murray, TE Max Klare and QB Ty Simpson inactive for Week 1 against the 49ers.
item.description:
Tutu Atwell

The Rams acquired Atwell via trade in August. Although he already knows the system, coach Sean McVay evidently feels that Atwell is unnecessary for this one. Incumbent QB Stetson Bennett has officially defeated Simpson for the QB2 job. Simpson is inactive, but has been labeled the emergency third quarterback.

Source: Nate Atkins

item.title: 49ers declared RB Jordan James inactive for Week 1 against the Rams.
item.description:
Jordan James SF Running Back

James has officially lost the backup job to rookie RB Kaelon Black, who should be safely stashed on fantasy benches before kickoff. The 49ers also declared QB Kurtis Rourke, CB Ephesians Prysock, WR Jordan Watkins, LB Tatum Bethune and OT Enrique Cruz inactive for Week 1 against the Rams.

Source: Matt Maiocco

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports that Patriots WR A.J. Brown (ankle) will miss at least four weeks.
item.description:
A.J. Brown NE Wide Receiver

NFL insider Jordan Schultz puts Brown’s return timeline between 3 and 6 weeks. Both reports make Brown a candidate to be placed on short-term injured reserve. The rest of the Patriots’ wide receiver corps failed to step up in Week 1. Newcomer WR Romeo Doubs will undoubtedly be given a chance to earn his hefty contract in Week 2.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: The Milwaukee Journal Sentinel’s Tom Silverstein reports that the Packers and TE Tucker Kraft are unlikely to agree on a contract extension before the season opener.
item.description:
Tucker Kraft GB Tight End

Silverstein believes the deal’s total value likely isn’t as important to the Packers as the structure. Kraft is still likely to reset the tight end market, but since he is returning from a season-ending ACL tear and has “yet to show he’s picked up where he left off last year, it may take some time for the deal to come together.” In the meantime, as long as he takes the field, Kraft can be treated as a TE1.

Source: Milwaukee Journal Sentinel

item.title: Cardinals RB Jeremiyah Love (ankle) was limited on Thursday.
item.description:
Jeremiyah Love ARI Running Back

Love is on track to play in Week 1 against the Chargers, though he could rotate in behind RB Tyler Allgeier, the team’s nominal starter. Earlier today, ESPN’s Adam Schefter said “it looks like” Love is going to be active for the season opener, though he stopped short of declaring it. Love would be a FLEX starter or better if active.

Source: Arizona Cardinals

item.title: Steelers CB Joey Porter (back) was limited on Thursday.
item.description:
Joey Porter PIT Cornerback

Porter is still on track to play in Week 1 against the Falcons. Whether his limitations are truly injury-related or contract-related is anyone’s guess. The team will tell us his status tomorrow.

Source: Pittsburgh Steelers

item.title: Bengals CB DJ Turner (hamstring) was limited on Thursday.
item.description:
DJ Turner CIN Cornerback

Defensive injuries aren’t always notable. This one is. Turner, 25, is an up-and-coming star defender, capable of challenging No. 1 wide receivers. If he is absent on Sunday, Buccaneers wide receivers will have a far easier time getting open.

Source: Paul Dehner Jr.

item.title: Buccaneers RB Sean Tucker (hamstring) was limited on Thursday.
item.description:
Sean Tucker TB Running Back

The Buccaneers’ No. 3 running back is only a bench stash at this time, but he could take on a few touches if he is active against the Bengals this weekend. He should be considered questionable to play at this time.

Source: Tampa Bay Buccaneers

item.title: Buccaneers WR Jalen McMillan (knee) was limited on Thursday.
item.description:
Jalen McMillan TB Wide Receiver

McMillan is on track to face the Bengals on Sunday, but he is clearly still ramping up post-injury, potentially adding volatility to his Week 1 outlook. The Buccaneers’ No. 3 wide receiver is a boom-bust FLEX.

Source: Tampa Bay Buccaneers

item.title: Chargers WR Brenen Thompson (hip) was limited on Thursday.
item.description:
Brenen Thompson LAC Wide Receiver

Brenen should be available on Sunday, but the Chargers could choose to keep their presumed No. 4 wide receiver under wraps until he is fully healthy. The rookie wide receiver will be relevant in single-game DFS tournaments once he is up to speed.

Source: Los Angeles Chargers

item.title: Chargers RB Keaton Mitchell (hamstring) was limited on Thursday.
item.description:
Keaton Mitchell LAC Running Back

If active, Mitchell will be an RB4. The Chargers’ talented running back group goes three-deep, so there is no reason to rush the speedy player back. That said, consecutive limited sessions put Mitchell on track to face the Cardinals on Sunday.

Source: Los Angeles Chargers

item.title: Commanders RB Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) was limited on Thursday.
item.description:
Jacory Croskey-Merritt WAS Running Back

The Commanders’ starting running back is on track to play, but it would be nice to see him practice fully tomorrow. If he is unable to do so, he might end up sharing more touches than he normally would with receiving RB Rachaad White. Croskey-Merritt supposedly refined his passing game skill set this summer, potentially raising his fantasy-scoring ceiling. Stay tuned.

Source: Adam Caplan

item.title: Eagles TE Eli Stowers (hamstring) was limited on Thursday.
item.description:
Eli Stowers PHI Tight End

Stowers had a rough training camp and has been sidelined since late August by the hamstring injury. He does not need to be rostered in 12-team leagues.

Source: Adam Caplan

item.title: Broncos WR Marvin Mims (foot) is practicing in full for Week 1 against the Chiefs.
item.description:
Marvin Mims DEN Wide Receiver

We assumed this would be the case, but we are happy to have it confirmed. Mims exited the Broncos’ preseason game against the Vikings on August 28th, and updates on the foot injury have been tough to find. The team named him a starter in three-wide receiver sets yesterday, which was a good sign. He is a boom-bust FLEX, per usual.

Source: Mike Klis

item.title: Chiefs WR Xavier Worthy (shoulder) is practicing in full for Week 1 against the Broncos.
item.description:
Xavier Worthy KC Wide Receiver

Worthy’s range of potential outcomes remains quite wide. The team attributed his lackluster 2025 season to the significant shoulder injury he suffered in Week 1. He missed time in training camp with a shoulder issue as well. He can be treated as a volatile FLEX playing in a top-tier offense against the Broncos.

Source: Kansas City Chiefs

item.title: Chiefs WR Rashee Rice (knee) is practicing in full for Week 1 against the Broncos.
item.description:
Rashee Rice KC Wide Receiver

Rice is evidently good to go for Week 1 after a tumultuous offseason, which included a knee operation and a jail stint. The Chiefs’ No. 1 wide receiver looked sluggish in training camp while rookie WR Cyrus Allen shined, but Rice’s status as the entrenched top target earner counts for something. Rice should be viewed as a WR2 entering the season.

Source: Kansas City Chiefs

item.title: Chiefs QB Patrick Mahomes (knee) is practicing in full for Week 1 against the Broncos.
item.description:
Patrick Mahomes KC Quarterback

Earlier this week, Chiefs coach Andy Reid said there is a “good chance” that Mahomes starts in Week 1. At this point, we would be surprised if he didn’t. The Chiefs’ quarterback is coming off season-ending ACL and LCL tears and will likely scramble less frequently than he did last year, potentially hurting his expected fantasy football output. He is a borderline QB1/2 against the Broncos’ elite defense.

Source: Kansas City Chiefs

item.title: Jaguars WR Jakobi Meyers (thumb) was limited on Thursday.
item.description:
Jakobi Meyers

Meyers said yesterday afternoon that he will play in Week 1, and we believe him. We would just like to see him upgrade to full participation tomorrow, if possible. The Jaguars field a deep wide receiver corps and Meyers appears to be jockeying for the No. 2 spot in the target pecking order with X-WR Brian Thomas. Assuming he is active, Meyers is FLEX-viable against the Browns in Week 1.

Source: Mary Kay Cabot

item.title: Packers coach Matt LaFleur said the team needs Christian Watson, Jayden Reed and Matthew Golden “out there for as many plays as humanly possible.”
item.description:
Christian Watson GB Wide Receiver

Prior reports indicated that the Packers’ coaching staff realized that their frequent wide receiver rotation was rubbing their stars the wrong way, prompting a positional personnel churn this offseason. LaFleur’s comments confirm the Packers’ starting wide receiver trio is going to play a lot, and fantasy managers should take note. Watson played extremely well in his recent from an ACL tear last year. If that play carries over, he is a shoo-in WR2 with substantial upside. Golden could be in for a Year 2 leap, and Reed could reliably return FLEX value, or better, if his snap share is high enough.

Source: Matt Schneidman

item.title: Jaguars RB LeQuint Allen (hip) was limited on Thursday.
item.description:
LeQuint Allen

Jaguars coach Liam Coen said yesterday that Allen would be a game-time decision for Week 1 against the Browns. If active, he should handle his typical pass-protection duties. If he is inactive, running backs Ameer Abdullah, Chris Rodriguez and Bhayshull Tuten could all take on a little extra work, though projecting the exact usage is challenging.

Source: Mary KayC abot

item.title: Ravens DT Nnamdi Madubuike (neck) was limited on Thursday.
item.description:
Nnamdi Madubuike BAL Defensive Lineman

Madubuike is seemingly on track to debut with his teammates, though his limited practice participation could result in limited snaps on game day. The interior game-wrecker is returning from a serious neck injury. Even playing on a snap count, Madubuike can make his presence felt.

Source: Adam Caplan

item.title: 49ers HC Kyle Shanahan told reporters that Kyle Tonges suffered and MCL injury against the Rams.
item.description:
Jake Tonges SF Tight End

Shanahan told reporters that it “doesn’t look good.” The 27-year-old tight end suffered the injury near the end of the first half, and it sounds like San Francisco will be without the backup tight end for some time. Luke Ferrell will likely see more snaps with Tonges unavailable.

Source: Matt Lively

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: Davante Adams caught 3-of-6 targets for 26 yards in the Rams’ Week 1 loss to the 49ers.
item.description:
Davante Adams

There was much talk about how great Adams looked in the precursor to the season, but it wasn’t on display in Week 1. The 33-year-old had a long gain of just 13 yards, and he and Matthew Stafford were unable to find much opening against the San Francisco secondary. Adams will get a chance to rebound in Week 2 in a Monday Night Football contest against the Giants.

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: George Kittle caught 2-of-5 targets for 12 yards in the 49ers’ Week 1 win over the Rams.
item.description:
George Kittle SF Tight End

Brock Purdy tried to get Kittle involved early in the contest, but it was the one legitimate option that Purdy wasn’t able to find success will. It’s amazing that the 32-year-old was even able to play in this game considering he tore his Achilles in January, but it is also fair to say it was a fantasy dud. Expect better things going forward for Kittle, and the next chance comes in Week 2 against a not-so-great Dolphins’ defense.

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: Kaelon Black rushed 14 times for 65 yards in the 49ers’ Week 1 win over the Rams.
item.description:
Kaelon Black SF Running Back

It was Black’s NFL debut, and all things considered, it was a pretty good one. The former Indiana star had four more carries than Christian McCaffrey, and was much more involved in the rushing attack in the first half; although CMC was obviously a factor in the passing attack and Black had just one catch for five yards. It wasn’t the most impressive statline you’ll see from a debut, but there were definitely flashes that suggest success for the 24-year-old. Black and the 49ers will get a chance to face the Dolphins in Week 2.

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: Seahawks QB Sam Darnold suffered an “unusual muscle strain,” and injured reserve is not being considered at this time.
item.description:
Sam Darnold SEA Quarterback

The report comes from the Ringer’s Tom Pelissero, who adds that “there is no timetable” for Darnold’s recovery, which will be based on “how he feels and how he recovers.” Pelissero referred to QB Drew Lock as “the likely starter” for the Seahawks’ Week 2 game against the Cardinals.

Source: Tom Pelissero

item.title: Giants WR Malik Nabers (knee) told reporters that it is his call whether he suits up or sits out in Week 1 against the Cowboys.
item.description:
Malik Nabers NYG Wide Receiver

Nabers fielded quite a few questions from reporters this afternoon, with many focusing on who makes the decision for him to play and whether he will be on a snap count. Nabers was adamant that his participation level is entirely his call. Of course, he chose not to share whether he is leaning toward playing or delaying his return, but noted that he is keeping his long-term health and career in mind. Nabers continues to practice in full, and ESPN’s Adam Schefter said earlier today that Nabers is “on track to play.” We lean that way as well, but his usage is tough to project. He is likely best viewed as a WR2 if active.

Source: SNY Giants

item.title: Colts WR Alec Pierce (heel) was limited on Thursday.
item.description:
Alec Pierce IND Wide Receiver

Pierce is technically on track to play, but his continued practice limitations suggest he is still ramping up. If active on Sunday, he would be a boom-bust FLEX, though having him on the field would be a big boost for his teammates. Pierce’s downfield abilities help keep safeties honest, freeing up the short-to-intermediate field depths.

Source: Adam Caplan

item.title: Ravens WR Zay Flowers (hamstring) practiced in full on Thursday.
item.description:
Zay Flowers BAL Wide Receiver

This is great news. The Ravens’ No. 1 wide receiver should be good to go for fantasy football WR2 duties against the Colts on Sunday. Flowers should log another full session tomorrow, barring a setback. He told reporters yesterday that he is feeling “better than ever.” That now appears to be the case.

Source: Adam Caplan

item.title: Saints RB Alvin Kamara (knee) was limited again on Thursday.
item.description:
Alvin Kamara NO Running Back

The Saints’ presumed passing down specialist is on track to play. Kamara sprained an MCL on August 18th, but the rehab is evidently going well. It is unclear whether Kamara could rotate in when the offense enters scoring position. Consider him a PPR FLEX option.

Source: Mike Triplett

item.title: Saints TE Oscar Delp (hamstring) was not seen practicing on Thursday.
item.description:
Oscar Delp NO Tight End

Delp is almost assuredly going to be ruled out tomorrow. The rookie tight end was unlikely to meaningfully challenge TE Juwan Johnson for targets early in the year, and the hamstring strain only reinforces that.

Source: Mike Triplett

item.title: Falcons WR Zachariah Branch (hamstring) was limited on Thursday.
item.description:
Zachariah Branch ATL Wide Receiver

The Falcons’ third-round rookie wide receiver could end up playing this week, but his inability to practice fully will keep him in a pure backup role. Branch does not need to be rostered in 12-team leagues.

Source: Atlanta Falcons

item.title: Falcons QB Tua Tagovailoa was added to the injury report with an oblique injury on Thursday.
item.description:
Tua Tagovailoa ATL Quarterback

Tagovailoa was seen grabbing at his back before removing himself from team drills earlier today. It turns out he is dealing with an oblique issue. The media viewing session ended before the Falcons began team drills, so it was unclear whether he rejoined his teammates. Backup QB Cooper Rush later told reporters that he took all first-team reps thereafter. Tagovailoa is now firmly in the questionable column for Week 1.

Source: Atlanta Falcons

item.title: Falcons QB Cooper Rush said he took all first-team reps in practice on Thursday.
item.description:
Cooper Rush ATL Quarterback

Earlier today, we learned that the Falcons’ Week 1 starting QB Tua Tagovailoa removed himself from individual drills with an apparent back injury. A report shortly after practice revealed that he suffered an oblique injury. As things currently stand, Rush should probably be treated as the expected starter for the Falcons’ Week 1 game against the Steelers. He is a low-end QB2.

Source: Marc Raimondi

item.title: The Athletic’s Dan Wiederer reports that there is “growing optimism” regarding OT Ozzy Trapilo’s (knee) “accelerated timeline.”
item.description:
Ozzy Trapilo CHI Offensive Lineman

Bears OL coach Dan Roushar adds that the team would “rather be a day too late than a day too early” with Trapilo, but it sounds like the young offensive tackle could join his teammates in team drills soon. The team has “confidence he can quickly return to the level he finished last season at.” That would be great news for the offense as a whole. The 2025 second-round pick produced a promising rookie season before rupturing his patellar tendon.

Source: Dan Wiederer

item.title: ESPN’s Rich Cimini reports Jets RB Breece Hall (groin) said he is “good to go and can handle a full workload, if necessary.”
item.description:
Breece Hall NYJ Running Back

It’s unclear whether Hall added the “if necessary” bit or if Cimini did, but regardless, this is good to hear. Hall is practicing in full leading up to the Jets’ Week 1 game against the Titans and can be treated as an RB1. Jets RB3 Isaiah Davis (knee) is also practicing fully.

Source: Rich Cimini

item.title: Bills RB Ty Johnson (hamstring) did not practice on Thursday.
item.description:
Ty Johnson BUF Running Back

It sure looks like the hamstring strain that Johnson suffered more than a month ago is going to keep him sidelined for the Bills’ season opener against the Texans. Starting RB James Cook was expected to play a larger role in the passing game this year. With Johnson sidelined, Cook could hog passing down snaps.

Source: Matt Parrino

item.title: Titans signed CB Jaylon Jones, formerly of the Colts.
item.description:
Jaylon Jones TEN Cornerback

The Colts waived Jones only two days ago. He now hops across the AFC South to Tennessee. The Titans correspondingly waived CB Melvin Smith Jr.

Source: Tennessee Titans

item.title: The Athletic’s Josh Kendall reports that Falcons QB Tua Tagovailoa “appeared to suffer discomfort” while throwing “and briefly went to the ground” on Thursday.
item.description:
Tua Tagovailoa ATL Quarterback

Tagovailoa reportedly “missed the first week of training camp due to lower back spasms.” Perhaps they are still an issue. Tagovailoa grabbed at his back before sitting down. After returning to his feet, he walked off the field and watched his teammates practice for the rest of the media’s viewing period. Tagovailoa is slated to start in Week 1 against the Steelers, though he is only a low-end QB2. The team named QB Cooper Rush as the primary backup in front of QB Jack Strand.

Source: Josh Kendall

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports that Packers RB Josh Jacobs remains on the Commissioner’s Exempt List and that there is “no timetable” as to when he could be disciplined.
item.description:
Josh Jacobs GB Running Back

The NFL is “closely monitoring all developments in the matter, which remains under review of the personal conduct policy.” We expect Jacobs to receive a suspension, but the league can move at its own pace. Packers RB MarShawn Lloyd is expected to serve as the fill-in starter.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports that Giants WR Malik Nabers (knee) is “on track to play” in Week 1 against the Cowboys.
item.description:
Malik Nabers NYG Wide Receiver

Nabers began the week practicing fully with his teammates, and we expect that to remain the case today and tomorrow. Giants coach John Harbaugh stopped short of saying Nabers will face the Cowboys in Week 1, but signs are certainly pointing toward that outcome. Hopefully, we get an indication as to whether the team plans to keep him on a snap count in the coming days.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter said “it looks like” Cardinals RB Jeremiyah Love (ankle) is going to play in Week 1 against the Chargers.
item.description:
Jeremiyah Love ARI Running Back

Love logged a limited session on Wednesday, and veteran RB Tyler Allgeier was listed as the team’s starter on the official depth chart. That said, the No. 3 overall pick can not simply be relegated to a pure backup role if healthy. As long as Love is practicing fully by Friday, he should be in fantasy lineups as a FLEX starter at worst.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter said Raiders RB Ashton Jeanty (ankle) is going to play in Week 1 against the Dolphins.
item.description:
Ashton Jeanty LV Running Back

This appeared to be the case yesterday, with Jeanty practicing in full to begin the week. It’s still nice to hear Schefter confirm as much, though. While Jeanty nursed his sprained ankle, rookie RB Mike Washington showed out in preseason play, leading NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport to report that Washington is “going to be a thing this year.” Jeanty should be treated as a fantasy RB1, but Washington warrants FLEX treatment, particularly against a rebuilding Dolphins defense this week.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports that the projection of Brock Bowers missing one or two weeks “is coming essentially from people around him.”
item.description:
Brock Bowers LV Tight End

Even though Schefter was the first to report that Bowers was expected to miss a game or two, he’s seemingly walking that back now. Speaking on The Pat McAfee Show, he went on to say that a player dealing with this type of injury is always going to downplay the severity. Schefter also noted that even if Bowers is back in two weeks, it’s not realistic to expect him at full strength in two weeks. Long story short, Schefter is casting a lot of doubt on both the timeline for Bowers to return and his ability to produce when he comes back. Bowers has been dealing with knee issues since the start of the 2025 season, and this unexpected setback could not have come at a worse time. Michael Mayer will start until he is healthy. Mayer begins the year as a mid-range TE2 versus Miami.

Source: The Pat McAfee Show

item.title: NewOrleans.Football’s Nick Underhill believes Alvin Kamara (knee) will play in Week 1 against the Lions.
item.description:
Alvin Kamara NO Running Back

Underhill did note that Kamara needs to make it to Sunday without any setbacks. He was limited in practice on Wednesday after suffering an MCL injury during a training camp scrimmage. The initial timeline for his return would have seen him miss multiple weeks of the regular season, but Kamara is well ahead of schedule in his recovery. He will likely serve as a passing-downs specialist with Travis Etienne handling the bulk of the carries.

Source: Nick Underhill

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the Seahawks believe they “dodged a bullet” with Sam Darnold’s hip injury.
item.description:
Sam Darnold SEA Quarterback

Darnold underwent tests last night that ruled out a hip fracture. He went in for an MRI this morning, and the team’s medical staff is still trying to determine how much time he will miss. Still, the outcome is overall positive given that a season-ending injury looks unlikely at this point. Ian Rapoport later added that Darnold will miss Week 2 but could only miss a few weeks. Drew Lock will start for Seattle until Darnold is healthy. Lock threw for 187 yards and a score in relief of Darnold last night. He was only sacked once and did not turn the ball over. As long as he keeps that up, the Seahawks will be able to stay afloat on the back of their elite defense.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: The Athletic’s Matt Schneidman reports Josh Jacobs pleaded no contest to misdemeanor battery and criminal damage to property.
item.description:
Josh Jacobs GB Running Back

Jacobs’ trial was initially slated to take place on November 17th. That date was recently moved up to today, signaling that Jacobs wanted to wrap up his legal proceedings quickly. He has been on the Commissioner’s Exempt List since the end of training camp. Roger Goodell could have kept him on the list indefinitely, especially with the trial previously scheduled multiple months into the season. With the legal matter now settled, Jacobs will likely serve a minor suspension as a result of the charges. MarShawn Lloyd is expected to handle the bulk of the carries until he returns.

Source: Matt Schneidman

item.title: ESPN’s Dan Graziano believes Pat Bryant “might force his way into a bigger role than expected.”
item.description:
Pat Bryant DEN Wide Receiver

Graziano mentioned Bryant’s strong offseason as a reason to believe he could see more work in his second season. Bryant appeared to be gaining traction late in his rookie campaign before injuries brought his season to an underwhelming end. He finished the year with 31 grabs for 378 yards and one score. Bryant will top out as the Broncos’ No. 3 receiver to start the year, but he could push Courtland Sutton for targets and routes as the season progresses. His usage in Week 1 will be an important storyline for fantasy managers to monitor.

Source: ESPN

item.title: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler believes Jacoby Brissett “could be a trade candidate at midseason” if he is playing well and the Cardinals are losing games.
item.description:
Jacoby Brissett ARI Quarterback

Fowler notes that the Cardinals likely want to see what they have in Carson Beck before the season ends. Of course, if the Cardinals are winning games, they will stick with what is working. Brissett put up strong counting stats last year, throwing for 281 yards per game across his 12 starts. That, however, did not result in any success for the Cardinals, who went 1-11 with Brissett under center. A similar season would make the veteran a viable backup or injury fill-in at that trade deadline.

Source: ESPN

item.title: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports the “preliminary diagnosis” for A.J. Brown is a high-ankle sprain.
item.description:
A.J. Brown NE Wide Receiver

Garafolo added, “MRI today after X-rays were negative.” That’s a good sign, but there is currently no timeline for Brown’s return. It will ultimately be a multi-week injury that could linger well into the season. Demario Douglas led the Pats with seven targets last night, though his looks are generally low-value check-downs. Mack Hollins and Romeo Doubs will serve as the team’s primary outside receivers until Brown is healthy. Hollins led the Pats in receiving yards at a modest 51. Hollins is worth adding in deeper leagues, but it’s hard to imagine him putting up anything more than WR4 numbers while Brown is sidelined. Doubs should improve in Week 2 after failing to catch any of his three targets versus the Seahawks. He will get another shot at WR3 numbers against Pittsburgh next week.

Source: Mike Garafolo

item.title: A.J. Brown (ankle) was seen wearing a boot in the locker room after the Patriots’ Week 1 loss to the Seahawks.
item.description:
A.J. Brown NE Wide Receiver

Romeo Doubs said to reporters after the game that Brown told teammates, “Everything was going to be alright.” He added that Brown was doing really well. Brown had his ankle rolled on while going to the ground in the third quarter of last night’s game. He immediately grabbed his ankle in pain and eventually limped off the field. New England ruled him out after a trip to the locker room. It sounds like a high-ankle sprain, which would sideline Brown for at least a few weeks. Mack Hollins and Romeo Doubs will both play more in his absence. Demario Douglas, who led the team with seven targets in Week 1, will also see more work.

Source: Boston Herald

item.title: George Kittles (Achilles) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 1 against the Rams.
item.description:
George Kittle SF Tight End

Kittle has made a remarkably quick recovery from the Achilles tear he suffered in the Wild Card Round. He is good to go just eight months later, and all reports out of training camp said he still looks as explosive as ever. We will need to see what he looks like in live action to confirm that, but it’s an impressive recovery nonetheless. Kittle could be on a snap count this week as the 49ers ramp him up to full speed, dropping him lower in the fantasy rankings than normal. He is a low-end TE1 for the 49ers’ Australia showdown with the Rams.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: A.J. Barner caught both of his targets for 13 yards in the Seahawks’ Week 1 win over the Patriots.
item.description:
AJ Barner SEA Tight End

Barner also had a tush push attempt that was called back by a penalty. With Jaxon Smith-Njigba soaking up 11 targets on just 24 team pass attempts, there wasn’t much volume to go around for the rest of the Seattle pass-catchers. Barner only topped four catches in 20 combined regular and postseason appearances last year. If Week 1 is any indication, he won’t be putting up big box scores very often this season either. He will barely crack the TE2 ranks when Seattle takes on Arizona next week.

item.title: Rashid Shaheed caught 1-of-3 targets for four yards in the Seahawks’ Week 1 win over the Patriots.
item.description:
Rashid Shaheed SEA Wide Receiver

Shaheed caught multiple passes in 4-of-12 games as a Seahawk last year. He stayed the course in Week 1 with another single-catch outing. Shaheed simply can’t earn targets in an offense that revolves around getting Jaxon Smith-Njigba the ball at all levels. His versatility and elite skills on both punt and kick returns are valuable for the Seahawks in real life, but they don’t put fantasy points on the table. He is not on the FLEX menu headed into Week 2.

item.title: Cooper Kupp caught 2-of-3 targets for 35 yards in the Seahawks’ Week 1 win over the Patriots.
item.description:
Cooper Kupp SEA Wide Receiver

Kupp had one of the highlights of the night with a leaping, one-handed snag late in the third quarter. The 24-yard catch eventually resulted in a field goal and Seattle’s first points of the night. Kupp can still come up with the occasional clutch play, but his ability to earn targets is all but gone. With Drew Lock likely filling in for an injured Sam Darnold next week, Kupp is not on the fantasy radar ahead of Week 2.

item.title: George Holani rushed eight times for 29 yards in the Seahawks’ Week 1 win over the Patriots.
item.description:
George Holani SEA Running Back

Holani forced a true committee with first-round rookie Jadarian Price, only seeing two fewer carries than him. Emanuel Wilson also mixed in for a pair of rushes. Holani served as the team’s primary back on third and fourth downs, but he was only targeted once and ultimately ran fewer routes than Price. With a much more favorable matchup versus Arizona on tap, Holani will have some low-end FLEX appeal next week.

item.title: Jadarian Price rushed 10 times for 52 yards in the Seahawks’ Week 1 win over the Patriots, adding two catches for six yards.
item.description:
Jadarian Price SEA Running Back

Price looked the part of a first-round running back, turning his first career carry into a 13-yard gain. He averaged 5.2 yards per carry compared to just 3.6 for George Holani. The bad news is that Holani saw eight carries and was the team’s trusted option in several key situations. Price did not play on a single third or fourth down. He saw just one of the Seahawks’ three short-yardage carries. Price is going to struggle to put up solid fantasy numbers if he can’t earn high-value touches. There’s plenty of time for that to change over the course of his rookie season, but he will be stuck in the RB3 ranks for his Week 2 date with the Cardinals.

item.title: Eli Raridon caught his only target for two yards and a touchdown in the Patriots’ Week 1 loss to the Seahawks.
item.description:
Eli Raridon NE Tight End

Raridon caught the first touchdown of the 2026 season on a goal line toss from Drake Maye. The Pats showed a lot of 12-personnel looks early in the game, but that faded in the second half, especially once A.J. Brown left the game with an ankle injury. Raridon isn’t on the fantasy radar yet, but his minor role could prove costly for Hunter Henry, who was held to three targets today.

item.title: Hunter Henry caught all three of his targets for 26 yards in the Patriots’ Week 1 loss to the Seahawks.
item.description:
Hunter Henry NE Tight End

Henry was quiet in this contest, though the same can be said of basically every member of New England’s passing attack. Despite losing A.J. Brown to an ankle injury, Henry’s role didn’t change. He earned a measly nine percent target share and ceded a handful of routes to rookie tight end Eli Raridon, who scored on his only target of the day. Henry will remain in the TE2 ranks for Week 2, but another quiet day will raise red flags for fantasy managers.

item.title: Demario Douglas caught 5-of-7 targets for 20 yards in the Patriots’ Week 1 loss to the Seahawks.
item.description:
DeMario Douglas NE Wide Receiver

Seattle shut down the Patriots’ deep passing game, forcing Drake Maye to pepper Douglas with low-value check-downs. Douglas wound up leading the Pats in targets and catches. He finished fifth in receiving yards. With A.J. Brown banged up, Douglas could be in line for another smattering of targets next week versus the Steelers. Even with Brown out, Douglas would barely register as a PPR WR5.

item.title: Romeo Doubs failed to catch any of his three targets in the Patriots’ Week 1 loss to the Seahawks.
item.description:
Romeo Doubs NE Wide Receiver

Doubs was blanketed in coverage all night. He failed to climb the ladder and win a jump ball early in the fourth quarter, resulting in a deflected ball turning into an interception. Later in the quarter, Doubs turned his eyes upfield before securing the pass and let the ball slip out of his hands for a drop. Drake Maye was intercepted on the next play. By any measure, this was a catastrophic debut for a player who signed a four-year, $68 million contract in the offseason. The good news for Doubs is that the team will likely be counting on him to step up next week. A.J. Brown left this game with an ankle injury and did not return. If he isn’t available for Week 2 versus the Steelers, Doubs will get one more chance at a WR3 fantasy ranking.

item.title: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said Sam Darnold underwent tests that ruled out a hip fracture.
item.description:
Sam Darnold SEA Quarterback

Darnold will undergo more testing tomorrow to gain more info on the hip injury he suffered in the first quarter of Seattle’s Week 1 win over New England. The good news is that a season-ending hip fracture has been ruled out, though there are still other serious injuries on the table. Drew Lock will start for the Seahawks until Darnold is able to return. Lock threw for 187 yards and a score in the team’s win over the Pats.

Source: Tom Pelissero

item.title: Mack Hollins caught 4-of-5 passes for 51 yards in the Patriots’ Week 1 loss to the Seahawks.
item.description:
Mack Hollins NE Wide Receiver

Hollins got on the field plenty early in the game, but his snaps were heavily tilted toward blocking duties. Once A.J. Brown went down with an ankle injury, the Pats were forced to play him in a more traditional role. He wound up leading the team in receiving yards, though that largely speaks to the Pats’ struggles through the air. Hollins would be in line for more work if Brown is unable to suit up next week. He would be a low-end WR5 sans Brown, making him a low-wattage add off the waiver wire.

item.title: Corey Kiner rushed six times for 11 yards in the Patriots’ Week 1 loss to the Seahawks.
item.description:
Corey Kiner NE Running Back

Kiner served as Rhamondre Stevenson’s backup with TreVeyon Henderson out this week. He was the only other Pats running back to see a carry in this game, though practice squad call-up Lan Larison was targeted twice, both of which he caught. Kiner did not see a look through the air. As a backup running back without any pass-catching value, Kiner is not on the fantasy radar heading into Week 2.

item.title: Rhamondre Stevenson rushed 18 times for 51 yards in the Patriots’ Week 1 loss to the Seahawks, adding five catches for 44 yards.
item.description:
Rhamondre Stevenson NE Running Back

With TreVeyon Henderson sidelined, Stevenson ceded just six attempts to backup Corey Kiner and two catches to practice squad call-up Lan Larison. That’s the good news. The bad news is that he was atrocious on the ground, averaging 2.8 yards per carry. New England rolled out a fairly predictable ground game versus the Seahawks, running on early downs with obvious run-focused personnel groups. That made Seattle’s job of bottling up Stevenson extremely easy. Drake Maye finished just four yards behind Stevenson despite running just seven times. As long as Henderson is out, Stevenson should hang out in the RB2 ranks based on his impressive workload. The efficiency should also improve next week when he takes on the Steelers.

item.title: Drew Lock completed 16-of-22 passes for 187 yards and a touchdown in the Seahawks’ 13-10, Week 1 win over the Patriots.
item.description:
Drew Lock SEA Quarterback

Lock took over for Sam Darnold after he suffered a hip injury at the end of Seattle’s opening drive. Darnold was initially listed as questionable to return but was ruled out for good just before halftime. Lock acquitted himself well, averaging 8.5 yards per attempt with just one sack. He also added two carries for 13 yards on the ground. Jaxon Smith-Njigba did most of the work for him with a 45-yard touchdown grab in the fourth quarter. All but four of the yards came after the catch. Still, Lock took care of the ball, peppered his best receiver with targets, and came away with the win. If Darnold is out for an extended period, Lock would be near the back of the QB2 mix for fantasy purposes. Superflex managers will want to take a flyer on him unless we get good news about Darnold over the next few days.

item.title: Drake Maye completed 23-of-33 passes for 178 yards, a touchdown, and three interceptions in the Patriots’ 13-10, Week 1 loss to the Seahawks.
item.description:
Drake Maye NE Quarterback

Maye once again struggled with Seattle’s ironclad defense, routinely making poor decisions when attempting to push the ball downfield. His third, and worst, interception of the night came when he lobbed a pass off his back foot at Mack Hollins with under 30 seconds left. The throw fell well short of his target and Josh Jobe made a toe-tapping pick in the end zone. Maye only threw multiple interceptions once last year, including the postseason. That came in his Super Bowl loss to the Seahawks. His multi-pick total is already at one this year, again at the hands of Seattle. It’s a long season, but Maye did nothing to silence the “schedule merchant” claims tonight. He will look to rebound as a mid-range QB1 versus the Steelers next week. That could be without A.J. Brown, who left this game with an ankle injury and did not return.

item.title: Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught 8-of-11 targets for 122 yards and a touchdown in the Seahawks’ Week 1 win over the Patriots.
item.description:
Jaxon Smith-Njigba SEA Wide Receiver

Sam Darnold went down with a hip injury on the first drive of the night. It took Drew Lock a couple of drives to dial in on JSN, but it was business as usual once he did. No Seahawk saw more than three targets aside from Smith-Njigba. He finished the night with a monstrous 41.7 percent target share. His highlight of the night wa sa 45-yard catch-and-run for Seattle’s only touchdown of the game. Even if Darnold misses time, JSN’s role is so fantasy-friendly that he will remain well inside the WR1 ranks for his Week 2 date with the Cardinals.

item.title: A.J. Brown suffered an ankle injury in Week 1 against the Seahawks and will not return.
item.description:
A.J. Brown NE Wide Receiver

A Seattle defender landed on Brown’s leg in the third quarter and the former Eagle clutched at his ankle as soon as he hit the ground. Brown eventually made his way off the field and limped to the locker room. He was listed as questionable for roughly a quarter, but the team has now ruled him out. The immediate worry will be that Brown suffered a dreaded high ankle sprain. That would sideline him for multiple weeks, though it’s too early to say much about the injury. Mack Hollins, Romeo Doubs, and Demario Douglas will all see some extra routes sans Brown.

item.title: A.J. Brown (ankle) is questionable to return in Week 1 against the Seahawks.
item.description:
A.J. Brown NE Wide Receiver

Brown had his ankle rolled on while attempting to corral a low pass in the third quarter. He limped off the field and went directly into the blue medical tent. He eventually walked into the locker room under his own power. Mack Hollins and Romeo Doubs will serve as New England’s primary outside wideouts while Brown is sidelined. Demario Douglas could also see some extra run out of the slot.

item.title: Sam Darnold suffered a hip injury in Week 1 against the Patriots and will not return.
item.description:
Sam Darnold SEA Quarterback

Darnold was slammed into the ground while being sacked on Seattle’s opening drive. He immediately went into the blue medical tent and was eventually listed as questionable to return. Seattle ruled him out just before the end of the first half. Drew Lock will stay under center for the remainder of the game. After putting up zero points during the first half, the fantasy outlook of every relevant Seattle pass-catcher will take a massive hit if this hip injury keeps Darnold on the sidelines beyond Week 1.

item.title: Sam Darnold (hip) is questionable to return to the Seahawks’ Week 1 game against the Patriots.
item.description:
Sam Darnold SEA Quarterback

Darnold suffered the injury while taking a sack on the opening drive of the game. He initially waved the training staff off but eventually went into the blue tent for further evaluation. The trainers escorted him to the locker room after his time in the tent. Drew Lock is under center for the Seahawks.

item.title: Cardinals RB Jeremiyah Love (ankle) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description:
Jeremiyah Love ARI Running Back

Head coach Mike LaFleur said earlier Wednesday that Love would have “no limit.” However, the rookie was indeed listed as limited for Wednesday’s practice report, likely as a formality. The ankle injury may limit him and prop up Tyler Allgeier for some work to open the year but the 21-year-old is a high-end RB2 for the full season. Love is trending in the right direction to play Week 1 against the Chargers.

item.title: Rams EDGE Myles Garrett (knee) was a full participant in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description:
Myles Garrett

As expected, Garrett gets in a full practice ahead of the Rams’ Week 1 Australia matchup against the 49ers. He did not practice Tuesday but it was likely a load management day for the star pass-rusher’s knee. Expect more of these kinds of practice weeks from Garrett moving forward; he is good to go for Week 1.

item.title: Raiders RB Ashton Jeanty (ankle) is practicing in full for Week 1 against the Dolphins.
item.description:
Ashton Jeanty LV Running Back

This is great news. Raiders coach Klint Kubiak told reporters earlier today that Jeanty would resume practicing today, however, we assumed it would be a limited session. It turns out Jeanty is already good to go. He faces a soft Dolphins defense in Week 1 and can be treated as a fantasy football RB1 even if rookie RB Mike Washington handles a decent workload as his backup/.

Source: Las Vegas Raiders

item.title: Seahawks S Nick Emmanwori (ankle) is inactive for Week 1 against the Patriots.
item.description:
Nick Emmanwori SEA Safety

Emmanwori underwent surgery to deal with an ankle issue back in July. Despite some limited practice participation, the 22-year-old is not yet ready to return. With S Ty Okada (hamstring) also out, the Seahawks will lack depth in the back of the secondary for Week 1 against the Patriots.

item.title: Seahawks WR Tory Horton (hamstring) is inactive for Week 1 against the Patriots.
item.description:
Tory Horton SEA Wide Receiver

Horton got in some limited practices earlier this week as he deals with a hamstring injury. He will miss opening week against the Patriots, boosting Rashid Shaheed for some deep targets in Week 1. Also inactive for the Seahawks are S Nick Emmanwori, G Beau Stephens, QB Jalen Milroe, TE Nick Kallerup, S Ty Okada, and DE Mike Morris. Milroe will serve as the emergency third quarterback.

Source: Seattle Seahawks

item.title: Patriots RB TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) is inactive for Week 1 against the Seahawks.
item.description:
TreVeyon Henderson NE Running Back

Henderson was ruled out with an ankle injury after not practicing all week. Rhamondre Stevenson will be the workhorse running back for New England, propelling him into the fantasy RB2 conversation. Also inactive for the Patriots are CB Karon Prunty, LB Erick Hunter, OT Walter Rouse, C Ben Brown, WR Efton Chism, and QB Behren Morton.

Source: New England Patriots

item.title: 49ers TE George Kittle (Achilles) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description:
George Kittle SF Tight End

Kittle gets in another limited practice ahead of the 49ers’ Week 1 Australia game against the Rams. We expect him to continue to get limited practices in beyond this week as the 32-year-old nurses his Achilles. Also limited was FB Kyle Juszczyk (finger). Both are still in line to play this week.

item.title: Eagles TE Eli Stowers (hamstring) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description:
Eli Stowers PHI Tight End

Stowers has been dealing with a hamstring injury he suffered in the preseason and he opens Week 1 with a limited practice. The 23-year-old rookie was already in line for a limited role this season after a subpar training camp but now may be limited even further with a soft tissue injury. Stowers is off fantasy radars in redraft leagues but his absence propels Dallas Goedert into borderline top-10 tight end territory.

item.title: Bears QB Tyson Bagent (back) did not participate in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description:
Tyson Bagent CHI Quarterback

Bagent popped up on the injury report with a back issue to open the week. He previously dealt with a hamstring issue but this appears to be a new injury. It’s unclear if the back will keep Bagent out of Week 1 just yet, but Case Keenum will step up at backup quarterback if he misses time.

item.title: Keaton Mitchell (hamstring) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description:
Keaton Mitchell LAC Running Back

Mitchell went down with the hamstring injury late in camp but returned to practice earlier this week. The team will likely keep his workload light in practice and on Sunday. Omarion Hampton remains the clear lead back in LA, with Mitchell mixing in for some designed touches. He will be an RB4 for his first game as a Charger.

item.title: Chargers WR Brenen Thompson (hip) was limited on Wednesday.
item.description:
Brenen Thompson LAC Wide Receiver

Thompson tweaked his hip in preseason play back on August 20th. A limited session on Wednesday puts him on track to play in Week 1 against the Cardinals, potentially as the team’s WR4 and a special teams contributor.

Source: Los Angeles Chargers

item.title: Tucker Kraft (knee) is not on the injury report ahead of his Week 1 game against the Vikings.
item.description:
Tucker Kraft GB Tight End

Kraft has been trending toward playing in Week 1 for a long time. Not appearing on the injury report in any capacity means he is good to go. Kraft may still have somewhat of a pitch count for his first game back from a 2025 torn ACL, but Matt LaFleur will be sure to get him the ball when he is on the field. Kraft is a fantasy TE1 for the Packers’ Week 1 game against Minnesota.

item.title: Commanders RB Rachaad White (hamstring) is practicing in full for Week 1 against the Eagles.
item.description:
Rachaad White WAS Running Back

White’s hamstring strain is officially behind him. The veteran running back is expected to assume passing down duties with his new team, though starting RB Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) has reportedly been improving his receiving skills this summer. If Croskey-Merritt can play this weekend, White will only be a mild FLEX play in PPR formats.

Source: Nicki Jhabvala

item.title: Commanders RB Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) was limited on Wednesday.
item.description:
Jacory Croskey-Merritt WAS Running Back

Getting in a limited session to begin the week puts Croskey-Merritt on track to start in Week 1 against the Eagles.
