The second-year running back has reportedly improved his passing game chops, but RB Rachaad White will likely be the team’s primary receiving back to begin the year. If Croskey-Merritt can siphon away receiving snaps, it will make him less reliant on positive game scripts. For now, if active, he is a borderline RB2/3.

Source: NickiJ habvala

item.title: Falcons QB Michael Penix (knee) is practicing in full for Week 1 against the Steelers.
item.description:
Michael Penix ATL Quarterback

Falcons coach Kevin Stefanski has already said Penix will be inactive this week, so this does not alter Penix’s game status. That said, it is still good to see him practicing fully. The Falcons are rolling with QB Tua Tagovailoa to begin the year, but his starting stint may not last long.

Source: Adam Caplan

item.title: Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur said there is “no limit” on Jeremiyah Love (ankle) in practice.
item.description:
Jeremiyah Love ARI Running Back

LaFleur left the door open for Love to be listed as limited on the injury report, but it sounds like that would be nothing more than a formality. He wouldn’t comit to Love playing in Week 1 just yet, but it sounds like things are headed in that direction. Love will likely split work with Tyler Allgeier to start the year, though he remains a far better bet in all fantasy formats.

Source: Bo Brack

item.title: Buccaneers WR Jalen McMillan (knee) was limited on Wednesday.
item.description:
Jalen McMillan TB Wide Receiver

The Buccaneers listed McMillan as a starter on the official depth chart yesterday, which is seemingly a vote of confidence regarding his availability this week. McMillan is on track to play, but will likely be limited to FLEX status in fantasy, playing behind WR Emeka Egbuka and WR Chris Godwin.

Source: Paul Dehner Jr.

item.title: Buccaneers WR Emeka Egbuka (toe) is practicing in full for Week 1 against the Bengals.
item.description:
Emeka Egbuka TB Wide Receiver

The Buccaneers had Egbuka take almost a month off to let the toe heal, which turned out to be a great call. The Buccaneers’ No. 1 wide receiver is good to go for Week 1. Nagging injuries slowed Egbuka’s rookie season. Entering 2026 in good health sets the stage for a bounce-back campaign. He is a WR2 with WR1 upside.

Source: Paul Dehner Jr.

item.title: Alvin Kamara (knee) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description:
Alvin Kamara NO Running Back

Kamara suffered an MCL injury during a scrimmage three weeks ago. The issue was initially expected to sideline him for at least a month, but it looks like he has a shot at significantly beating that timeline. Even if he doesn’t play this week, there’s a good chance Kamara is back by Week 2 or 3. He will be a low-end FLEX play in PPR leagues once he is healthy.

Source: Mike Garafolo

item.title: Bengals WR Tee Higgins (heel) is practicing in full for Week 1 against the Buccaneers.
item.description:
Tee Higgins CIN Wide Receiver

The Bengals will have their top two wide receivers on the field for what should be a high-scoring game against the Buccaneers. Higgins is a high-end WR2 with WR1 upside, playing alongside WR1 Ja’Marr Chase this weekend.

Source: Paul Dehner Jr.

item.title: Bengals WR Ja’Marr Chase (knee) is practicing in full for Week 1 against the Buccaneers.
item.description:
Ja'Marr Chase CIN Wide Receiver

Chase’s participation actually exceeds expectations. Beginning the week with a limited session would have been unsurprising. The Bengals’ star wide receiver hyperextended his knee on August 25th, but he is now good to go. Treat Chase as an elite WR1, per usual.

Source: Paul Dehner Jr.

item.title: Zachariah Branch (hamstring) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description:
Zachariah Branch ATL Wide Receiver

Branch ran behind Olamide Zaccheaus for most of training camp. A light workload in practice heading into Week 1 all but guarantees he won’t threaten the veteran receiver for a starting role to open the year. Branch isn’t on the fantasy radar for his NFL debut versus the Steelers.

item.title: Ravens DT Nnamdi Madubuike (neck) was limited on Wednesday.
item.description:
Nnamdi Madubuike BAL Defensive Lineman

Madubuike joined team drills last week, and is technically on track to play in Week 1 against the Colts. If active, the stud defensive tackle will likely be on a snap count, though the team could opt for a conservative approach and hold him out for this week.

Source: Jamison Hensley

item.title: Oscar Delp (hamstring) did not practice Wednesday.
item.description:
Oscar Delp NO Tight End

Delp has been out for multiple weeks with the hamstring issue. A DNP to open the season likely puts him on the wrong side of questionable. His absence will lock in Juwan Johnson as an every-down player, though that was barely a question even before this injury.

Source: Katherine Terrell

item.title: Ravens WR Zay Flowers (hamstring) was limited on Wednesday.
item.description:
Zay Flowers BAL Wide Receiver

For the record, Flowers told reporters that he is feeling “great” earlier today, but opted not to disclose his injury details. Now we know he is dealing with a soft tissue issue. Flowers is on track to play, but as is always the case with hamstrings, his practice participation is worth tracking. Ideally, he is practicing fully by Friday and can be treated as a WR2 on game day.

Source: Jamison Hensley

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports that Raiders TE Michael Mayer’s “role now is expected to grow” with TE Brock Bowers (knee) sidelined.
item.description:
Michael Mayer LV Tight End

Mayer, 25, immediately vaults into the TE1 tier, especially with a matchup against the Dolphins’ defense upcoming in Week 1. Mayer banked two top-five finishes last season, notably catching 9-of-10 targets for 89 yards in Week 17 with Bowers on injured reserve.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: Alec Pierce (heel) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description:
Alec Pierce IND Wide Receiver

Pierce is recovering from offseason surgery that caused him to miss the entirety of training camp and the preseason. The lack of reps could leave him a little rusty heading into Week 1, but the good news is that a limited practice today means he should be active versus the Ravens. Pierce will be a high-risk WR4 for the first slate of the season. Josh Downs and Tyler Warren were not on the injury report.

item.title: Jets TE Kenyon Sadiq (groin) is practicing fully for Week 1 against the Titans.
item.description:
Kenyon Sadiq NYJ Tight End

Sadiq is not yet ready for fantasy football TE1 duties, but he appears to have recovered from the setback he suffered in his rehab related to a hernia back in August. The Jets published their Week 1 depth chart earlier today with Sadiq listed as the backup behind TE Mason Taylor.

Source: Rich Cimini

item.title: Joey Porter Jr. (back) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description:
Joey Porter PIT Cornerback

Porter Jr. missed all of training camp with the back issue, though it’s widely believed that he was simply holding in while negotiating for a new contract. The team is likely working him up to full speed with today’s limited session. He should be good to go by Sunday for Pittsburgh’s date with the Falcons.

item.title: Jets RB Breece Hall (groin) is practicing fully for Week 1 against the Titans.
item.description:
Breece Hall NYJ Running Back

This news was expected, but it is great to see, regardless. Hall is set to handle a sizable, RB1-worthy workload this season, having been paid accordingly by the Jets’ front office back in May. The Titans field an unimposing defense. A ceiling outcome is in play for the veteran running back.

Source: Rich Cimini

item.title: Rome Odunze (calf) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description:
Rome Odunze CHI Wide Receiver

Bears coach Ben Johnson called Odunze “day to day” earlier this week. He went down with the calf injury in practice late last week. The initial reports were all positive, but it’s not a guarantee that Odunze will be ready for Week 1. A full practice over the next two days would be a good sign, though not necessary for Odunze to play. Assuming he does suit up, Odunze will be a high-riskF FLEX play.

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports that Raiders TE Brock Bowers is expected to miss “a game or two” after undergoing a meniscus trim on Tuesday.
item.description:
Brock Bowers LV Tight End

Raiders No. 2 TE Michael Mayer should be added wherever available. On the plus side, this does not appear to be a long-term absence, but missing Bowers for a couple of games is obviously concerning. According to Schefter, Bowers “got banged up ‘a little in camp’ and the injury was diagnosed last week.” With any luck, fantasy managers can expect to get their TE1 back for the Raiders’ Week 3 game against the Saints. Mayer is a TE1 in the meantime.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: Giants TE Theo Johnson (shoulder) is practicing fully for Week 1 against the Cowboys.
item.description:
Theo Johnson NYG Tight End

Johnson was seen practicing in a non-contact jersey last week, so today’s full session is positive. Unfortunately, Johnson’s path to fantasy football TE1 status is likely blocked by TE Isaiah Likely, so Johnson is not on the radar for most leagues.

Source: Adam Caplan

item.title: Cam Jordan (hamstring) will not play in Week 1 against the Lions.
item.description:
Cameron Jordan NO Defensive End

Jordan has been dealing with a hamstring issue for nearly a month. The fact that Kellen Moore was able to rule him out so early in the week suggests this issue could linger for much longer than just Sunday’s game. Jordan signed a one-year deal with stay in New Orleans for a 16th season in June. He totaled 10.5 sacks in 2025.

item.title: Jonathan Greenard (pec) practiced on Wednesday.
item.description:
Jonathan Greenard PHI Outside Linebacker

Eagles DC Vic Fangio said during training camp that Greenard could miss Week 1, so even a limited practice today is a good sign for the veteran EDGE. Philly traded for Greenard during the offseason and immediately signed him to a four-year, $100 million extension. The team will see how he responds to a week of practices before making a decision on his status before Sunday.

Source: Jeff McLane

item.title: Panthers RB Jonathon Brooks (groin) was limited on Wednesday.
item.description:
Jonathon Brooks CAR Running Back

Now we know what Brooks has been dealing with for the past week or so. Beginning the week with a limited session is a good sign regarding his Week 1 availability, but obviously we hope to see him practice fully as soon as possible, given his extensive injury history. He could end up rotating in behind RB Chuba Hubbard if active.

Source: Alex Zietlow

item.title: Malik Nabers (knee) practiced in full on Wednesday.
item.description:
Malik Nabers NYG Wide Receiver

Giants coach John Harbaugh told reporters he thinks Nabers is ready to go. Harbaugh didn’t fully commit to him playing in Week 1, but we would be stunned if Nabers isn’t out there on Sunday. Even if Nabers takes a few weeks to get back to form, he should be in fantasy lineups out of the gate. Nabers is, at worst, a high-end WR2 for his first game since suffering a torn ACL in Week 4 of the 2025 season.

Source: Connor Hughes

item.title: Panthers owner David Tepper declined to say whether the front office offered QB Bryce Young an extension this offseason.
item.description:
Bryce Young CAR Quarterback

Reporters first asked whether Young had received an offer from the team. Tepper passed on answering. A reporter then asked what would prompt the team to offer Young an extension. Tepper initially declined to answer once again, before adding, “but look, success is success. And you know it when you see it.” Anything is possible, but given those remarks, it seems plausible that no offer was made. The Panthers picked up Young’s fifth-year team option in April, keeping the 25-year-old quarterback under contract through 2027. This could be a make-or-break year for him as the starter, though.

Source: Alex Zietlow

item.title: Ravens WR Zay Flowers (undisclosed) said he feels “great” after practicing the past two days.
item.description:
Zay Flowers BAL Wide Receiver

Flowers was asked how he was feeling today while meeting with the press, with a beat reporter specifically asking Flowers about his quad. Flowers suffered a quad bruise early in training camp and missed time last week with an undisclosed injury. Now feeling “better than ever,” Flowers is seemingly on track to play in Week 1 against the Colts without issue.

Source: Jamison Hensley

item.title: Bills RB Ty Johnson (hamstring) was not present during the portion of practice open to the media.
item.description:
Ty Johnson BUF Running Back

Johnson went down while running a route on August 9th. He resumed running roughly two weeks ago, but has not yet rejoined his teammates in drills. Although Johnson is not on the fantasy radar himself, he has hogged passing down snaps in recent seasons. Starting RB James Cook has been expected to take on a larger receiving role this season, and Johnson’s potential absence adds credence to that idea.

Source: Katherine Fitzgerald

item.title: Kevin O’Connell said Carson Wentz will serve as Kyler Murray’s backup in Week 1.
item.description:
Carson Wentz MIN Quarterback

KOC didn’t mince words, saying, “This gives us the best chance to win this Sunday.” O’Connell did note that the backup quarterback decisions will be made on a week-to-week basis. Still, this serves as another indictment of J.J. McCarthy, who will presumably be inactive for Week 1. The former first-round pick is unlikely to play at all this year and will likely be looking for a new team after the season ends.

Source: Kevin Seifert

item.title: The Athletic’s Joe Buscaglia reports that Bills WR Khalil Shakir (undisclosed) is on the practice field on Wednesday.
item.description:
Khalil Shakir BUF Wide Receiver

This is good news. Shakir has been sidelined for multiple weeks, rehabbing an undisclosed injury. His return today puts him on track to play in Week 1 against the Texans’ top-tier defense. Whether Shakir can be a reliable FLEX with WR DJ Moore now in Buffalo and TE Dalton Kincaid reportedly set to take on a larger role remains to be seen. Getting back on the field is the first step, though.

Source: Joe Buscaglia

item.title: Parker Washington said his contract talks with the Jaguars “are continuing.”
item.description:
Parker Washington

Jags GM James Gladstone said last week that the team was open to an in-season extension with Washington, who is set to hit free agency next offseaosn. Both sides want to get a deal done, but they are clearly still at odds over the details of the contract. Even if it takes longer than expected, it does look like Washington will sign an extension before he gets to test the waters of free agency. Coming off an outstanding training camp, Washington should be treated as a fantasy WR2 for the Jags’ Week 1 date with the Browns.

Source: Ryan O’Halloran

item.title: Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said RB Ashton Jeanty (ankle) will practice on Wednesday.
item.description:
Ashton Jeanty LV Running Back

We expect this to be a limited session for the Raiders’ second-year running back. Jeanty has been sidelined since injuring his ankle on August 23rd. Returning for the week’s first official practice puts him on track to play, though the coaching staff could ease him into action in Week 1 against the Dolphins by giving rookie RB Mike Washington a little extra work this week. Hopefully, Jeanty is practicing fully by Friday, if not sooner.

Source: Ryan McFadden

item.title: Jakobi Meyers (hand) said he will play in Week 1 against the Browns.
item.description:
Jakobi Meyers

Meyers missed some time late in camp with a thumb injury. He wore a brace on his right hand late in training camp, causing some concern that the issue was more serious than initially expected. The brace was likely a precaution, as Meyers returned to practice a week ago. He will be in the FLEX mix versus the Browns this week.

Source: John Shipley

item.title: Buccaneers RB Sean Tucker (hamstring) did not practice on Wednesday.
item.description:
Sean Tucker TB Running Back

Buccaneers coach Todd Bowles said earlier this week that Tucker will be a game-time decision for Week 1 against the Bengals. His continued absence from practice is discouraging, but it bodes well for RB Bucky Irving and RB Kenneth Gainwell. Tucker is not expected to be a high-volume offensive contributor at this point, but adding even a couple of touches to each player’s workload is helpful

Source: Greg Auman

item.title: Jaguars coach Liam Coen said Cole Van Lanen (knee) will be a game-time decision for Week 1 against the Browns.
item.description:
Cole Van Lanen

Van Lanen suffered a serious knee injury in Week 18 last year and missed most of the offseason program. He practiced on Wednesday, though the team is still going to use the rest of the week to figure out if he’s ready for Week 1. Walker Little would likely take his spot in the lineup if he can’t go.

Source: Demetrius Harvey

item.title: Tyreek Hill’s agent Drew Rosenhaus said Hill’s doctors recommended he postpone his comeback until “perhaps some time in October.”
item.description:
Tyreek Hill

Rosenhaus gushed about Hill’s recovery and how he looks right now. He also mentioned that multiple teams asked him when Hill would be available to sign. We’ll take these with a few grains of salt, given Rosenhaus’s financial ties to his client. Hill is still working his way back from the catastrophic knee injury he suffered in Week 4 of the 2025 season. Fantasy managers can leave Hill on the waiver wire for now.

Source: The Pat McAfee Show

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Dae’Quan Wright “still is waiting to hear from the NFL about whether he is eligible to play this season.”
item.description:
Dae'Quan Wright

Wright was a UDFA this year. He signed with the Eagles, was cut, then joined the Browns. After Cleveland released him, Wright intended to rejoin LSU, becoming the first NFL player to return to college football. The SEC then passed a rule banning NFL players from returning. The NFL followed that up with a memo banning players who return to college football from signing in the NFL once again in the same year. As Schefter notes, Wright never officially signed with LSU, so he may be eligible to stay in the NFL after all. Wright is unfortunately caught in the middle of a legal nightmare brought on by the NCAA. It will likely prevent him from playing football anytime soon.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: Bengals coach Zac Taylor said Tee Higgins (heel) is on pace to play in Week 1 against the Bucs.
item.description:
Tee Higgins CIN Wide Receiver

Higgins has been dealing with a heel contusion recently, but the issue never seemed serious. He has still been able to practice in a limited capacity over the past week. He may ultimately be limited on the team’s first injury report of the season, but there’s almost no chance Higgins misses Week 1 versus the Bucs. He will be a boom/bust WR2 barring a setback.

Source: Andrew Siciliano

item.title: Bengals coach Zac Taylor said Ja’Marr Chase (knee) is on pace to play in Week 1 against the Bucs.
item.description:
Ja'Marr Chase CIN Wide Receiver

He said the same about Tee Higgins, who is dealing with a heel issue. Chase suffered a serious-looking knee injury late in camp, briefly giving Bengals fans and fantasy managers nightmares of him missing extended time. He was ultimately fine and should be good to go for Week 1, even if his participation in practice is limited. Per usual, Chase is in the WR1-overall mix versus the Bengals this week.

Source: Andrew Siciliano

item.title: Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley said there will be no “pitch count” for starting receiver Chris Bell, and that he trusts both Bell and fellow rookie starter Caleb Douglas.
item.description:
Chris Bell MIA Wide Receiver

“We believe those guys deserve to start, and we’re gonna start them,” was Hafley’s matter-of-fact Wednesday statement. His words come after the ‘Fins officially listed the third-round rookies as starters on Tuesday. His “pitch count” comments pertain to Bell’s summer stint on the NFI list as he completed his recovery from torn ACL suffered last season at Louisville. Starting a pair of Day 2 receivers in Week 1 is far from ideal for anybody, but no less so than trotting out Jalen Tolbert. The Dolphins are fully committed to their rebuild, and rookies like Bell, Douglas and Kevin Coleman are the biggest potential beneficiaries. Bell and Douglas belong on 12-team league watch lists, with Coleman worth a dynasty stash.

Source: Marcel Louis-Jacques

item.title: Cowboys placed LG Tyler Smith (thumb) on injured reserve.
item.description:
Tyler Smith DAL Guard

After undergoing surgery on his injured thumb, Smith will miss at least the first four weeks of the regular season. An All-Pro left guard, Smith started all 16 games he appeared in last season and proved to be a critical part of the Dallas offensive line. Fourth-year guard T.J. Bass is expected to start for the Cowboys while Smith recovers.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: The Tampa Bay Times’ Rick Stroud reports Emeka Egbuka (toe) “appears to be fine.”
item.description:
Emeka Egbuka TB Wide Receiver

Egbuka was seen practicing Wednesday ahead of the Bucs’ season opener against the Bengals and Stroud said there were no signs of injury for the second-year receiver, who has battled a toe injury in recent weeks. Barring any sort of setback, Egbuka should be in all fantasy lineups this week against the Bengals in what could be a high-scoring back-and-forth affair with Joe Burrow and company.

Source: Rick Stroud

item.title: Jets listed Mason Taylor as the team’s TE1 on the Week 1 depth chart.
item.description:
Mason Taylor NYJ Tight End

Taylor reportedly functioned as the Jets’ top tight end throughout training camp with Kenyon Sadiq (hernia) sidelined. Taylor, whose blocking ability recently drew praise from head coach Aaron Glenn, worked with Geno Smith two or three times a week in the offseason, developing chemistry with the veteran journeyman. Last year Taylor saw a target on 20 percent of his routes and logged a lowly 1.11 yards per route run in the low-octane New York offense. He’ll be a sneaky deep league option in Week 1 against the Titans.

Source: Brian Costello

item.title: Broncos listed J.K. Dobbins as the team’s RB1 on the team’s Week 1 depth chart.
item.description:
J.K. Dobbins DEN Running Back

Dobbins will once again start the season as Denver’s presumed lead back, though he’s unlikely to see much pass-game involvement. That should belong (for now) to RJ Harvey, who’s listed as the team’s RB2. Harvey last year was targeted on a strong 27 percent of his pass routes and ended the season with 47 receptions for 365 yards and six receiving scores. Rookie RB Jonah Coleman will start the year as the Broncos’ RB3. He profiles as a sneaky stash option in 12 and 14-team formats.

Source: Parker Gabriel

item.title: Broncos listed Marvin Mims, Jr. as a starting receiver for Week 1.
item.description:
Marvin Mims DEN Wide Receiver

Mims gets a starting slot alongside Courtland Sutton and Jaylen Waddle for the Broncos’ season opener against Kansas City. It’s quite the stunner after Pat Bryant — listed as a second-team wideout — drew consistent praise from Denver coaches this offseason both as an intermediate and downfield pass catcher. Mims, who has been used primarily as a gadget guy, was targeted on 20 percent of his routes last season and ended the year with 322 yards over 15 games. Bryant’s usage will be something to monitor in Week 1.

Source: Parker Gabriel

item.title: Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said RB LeQuint Allen (hip) is a game-time decision for Week 1 against the Browns.
item.description:
LeQuint Allen

As expected, Allen did not practice Wednesday. It’s not that fantasy managers were eager to start Allen this week, but his absence would open up more routes and potential targets for Bhayshul Tuten and Chris Rodriguez, who are listed as co-starters on Jacksonville’s Week 1 depth chart. Both C-Rod and Tuten would be slightly better options if Allen is sidelined this weekend.

Source: Ryan O’Halloran

item.title: Browns head coach Todd Monken said he’s confident in Deshaun Watson’s downfield passing ability.
item.description:
Deshaun Watson CLE Quarterback

Monken has stressed explosive plays as an important part of the Cleveland offense headed into the 2026 regular season. “Obviously having explosive players helps that,” Monken said. “Being able to scheme it up against certain looks and then being able to execute because your protection has to hold up when you get those opportunities. I’m confident in Deshaun and our ability to push the ball down the field, otherwise we wouldn’t be starting him.” That confidence might be misplaced considering Watson completed just 1-of-6 attempts for 20 yards and an interception on downfield passes in the preseason and was among the league’s worst deep ball passers in 2024, when he threw downfield on a career-low 27 percent of his attempts. Once an elite deep ball thrower, Watson will look to regain form coming off two torn Achilles, entering his age-30 season. Perhaps rookie WR Denzel Boston will be a boon for Watson’s downfield game in 2026.

Source: ESPN.com

item.title: Bills RB Ty Johnson (leg) was not present during the portion of practice open to the media.
item.description:
Ty Johnson BUF Running Back

Johnson went down while running a route on August 9th. He resumed running roughly two weeks ago, but has not yet rejoined his teammates in drills. Although Johnson is not on the fantasy radar himself, he has hogged passing down snaps in recent seasons. Starting RB James Cook has been expected to take on a larger receiving role this season, and Johnson’s potential absence adds credence to that idea.

Source: Katherine Fitzgerald

item.title: Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said RB LeQuint Allen (undisclosed) is a game-time decision for Week 1 against the Browns.
item.description:
LeQuint Allen

It’s not that fantasy managers were eager to start Allen this week, but his absence would open up more routes and potential targets for Bhayshul Tuten and Chris Rodriguez, who are listed as co-starters on Jacksonville’s Week 1 depth chart. Both C-Rod and Tuten would be slightly better options if Allen is sidelined this weekend.

Source: Ryan O’Halloran

item.title: 49ers DT Alfred Collins suffered a torn patellar tendon and is out for the 2026 season.
item.description:
Alfred Collins SF Defensive Tackle

Collins tore his patellar tendon during the 49ers’ first Australia practice last night. It’s an unfortunate break for the 2025 second-round pick, set to start Week 1 for the 49ers defensive line against the Rams. Collins’ biggest play last season was forcing a goal-line Kyren Williams fumble in Week 5. He will instead need knee surgery and begin a journey back from injury for 2027. The 49ers will reach into their defensive tackle depth and may activate Kevin Givens or Sebastian Valdez from the practice squad for Week 1 in Australia against the Rams.

Source: Matt Barrows

item.title: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports the Steelers made a contract extension offer to CB Joey Porter Jr.
item.description:
Joey Porter PIT Cornerback

According to Garafolo, the Steelers made an offer to Porter but it is “not good enough” for a contract extension to be imminent. This seems to be the first offer Pittsburgh has made to the 26-year-old, so there are at least negotiations happening. With both Devon Witherspoon and Christian Gonzalez getting top-of-market deals done, all eyes are on Porter as last among the big cornerback extensions to get done. Garafolo adds the Steelers will not negotiate into the season past Week 1, so both sides have a few days to get a deal done before talks are tabled until the end of the season.

Source: Mike Garafolo

item.title: Rams EDGE Myles Garrett (knee) did not participate in Tuesday’s practice.
item.description:
Myles Garrett

Garrett was a non-participant in practice Tuesday, but it looks to be a load management day with other Rams players listed as DNP due to rest and head coach Sean McVay saying Tuesday he expects Garrett to play Week 1. Though the team will be without Aaron Donald for opening day, the Rams are still expecting to have Garrett good to go against the 49ers.

item.title: 49ers TE George Kittle (Achilles) was limited in Tuesday’s practice.
item.description:
George Kittle SF Tight End

Kittle continues to work his way back from an Achilles tear in January and is seemingly on track to play Week 1. He practiced on Monday and gets in a limited practice again on Tuesday. Offensive coordinator Klay Kubiak was confident in Kittle’s availability this week, saying the 32-year-old looked good while the team practices in Australia. The entire 49ers offense practiced in some capacity Tuesday. Kittle’s chances of playing are trending upward; he’s a low-end TE1 if he plays against the Rams this week.

item.title: Buccaneers signed QB Baker Mayfield to a three-year, $165 million contract extension.
item.description:
Baker Mayfield TB Quarterback

The Buccaneers apparently reached out to Mayfield’s agent over the weekend; deadline do drive action after all. Mayfield is now under contract through his age-34 season. It’s not exactly a curious move for the Buccaneers — they didn’t have much of an avenue to find another quarterback given where they usually pick and rookie UDFA Jalon Daniels is their current backup. It is still a little surprising they let it twist in the wind as long as it did. Mayfield likely will be near the $50 million average annual value club once all the figures come in. (Some of this will be folded into the already-existing one-year contract.) He’ll be a reasonable superflex QB2 with a shot to rebound now that last year’s injuries are behind him.

Source: Mike Garafolo

item.title: Christian Barmore (knee) is not on New England’s final injury report for Week 1’s game against the Seahawks.
item.description:
Christian Barmore NE Defensive Tackle

He practiced in full on both Monday and Tuesday and seems set to go for the Wednesday opener. We’ll keep an eye on Barmore’s practice status going forward but the 27-year-old is definitely a candidate to get vet days this season.

item.title: Patriots RB TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) will not play in New England’s Week 1 game against the Seahawks.
item.description:
TreVeyon Henderson NE Running Back

Henderson did not practice at any point this week and should be considered questionable heading into Week 2’s games. Rhamondre Stevenson will get the bulk of the load against Seattle and should factor into the RB2 equation despite a tough matchup on paper. The Patriots also ruled out Ben Brown (knee), who did not travel with the team to Seattle.

item.title: Tory Horton (hamstring) is questionable for Seattle’s Week 1 game against the Patriots.
item.description:
Tory Horton SEA Wide Receiver

Even if Horton does play, he’s unlikely to be more than the fourth receiver behind Rashid Shaheed, Cooper Kupp and all-world Jaxon Smith-Njigba. The second-year receiver looked great early in 2025 but has dealt with a ton of injuries ever since, leading the Seahawks to their midseason trade for Shaheed last year.

item.title: Nick Emmanwori (ankle) is questionable for Seattle’s Week 1 game against the Patriots.
item.description:
Nick Emmanwori SEA Safety

One of Seattle’s other projected starters on defense, Ty Okada, was ruled out with a hamstring injury. It would certainly be a boon to Rhamondre Stevenson’s value if Emmanwori can’t go on Wednesday. Emmanwori had surgery on his ankle in July and opened camp on the PUP list. He’s generally been regarded as more doubtful-than-questionable, but there’s a chance he’s able to go based on this listing.

item.title: Rams coach Sean McVay said Myles Garrett (knee) will be ready to go for Week 1’s game against the 49ers.
item.description:
Myles Garrett

Heavily load-managed in the offseason, Garrett will enter his age-31 season fresh and ready to try to top last year’s 23-sack season in a new defense. We won’t be surprised if Garrett continues to be listed on the injury report going forward, but if he’s going to play through this there’s probably no need to be concerned about the report unless new concerns arise.

Source: Stu Jackson

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Aaron Donald will be inactive and won’t travel with the team in Week 1.
item.description:
Aaron Donald

He’s still “working himself into football shape,” per Rapoport and Adam Schefter. We think the Rams D/ST will manage with merely Myles Garrett and Trent McDuffie as major additions heading into Week 1’s showdown with the 49ers in Australia.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: The Athletic’s Jeff Zrebiec reports “multiple teams” reached out with interest in trading for Joe Fagnano after the preseason.
item.description:
Joe Fagnano BAL Quarterback

Fagnano completed 56-of-75 passes for 509 yards and three touchdowns in preseason action while taking just one sack. Last year’s major UDFA winner among the quarterbacks was Max Brosmer, so don’t go thinking Fagnano needs to be on your dynasty bench or anything, but him making the 53-man roster was interesting and this adds a little flavor as to why that was.

item.title: Dolphins wideout Chris Bell is listed as a starting wideout in Miami’s offense on their unofficial Week 1 depth chart.
item.description:
Chris Bell MIA Wide Receiver

Bell is yet another young wideout in Miami — along with Caleb Douglas — who could make a fantasy impact right away as the Dolphins deal with what looks on paper to be an extremely rough defense. Bell only just shed his non-contact jersey in late August, so we’re expecting a slow start, but his Week 1 performance could certainly throw him on waiver wire columns if he starts and plays most of the snaps.

Source: David Furones

item.title: Sports Illustrated’s John Shipley believes neither Bhayshul Tuten nor Chris Rodriguez will emerge as the lead back in 2026.
item.description:
Bhayshul Tuten

Shipley hedges a bit by noting that there’s a chance that one back simply carries the momentum early in the season forward and never lets up, but ultimately falls on the idea that neither back is likely to hit 1,000 rushing yards in 2026. “I think there is a more likely chance we see both running backs hit 750+ yards than one of them hit 1,000,” Shipley writes. Such a split would probably lean towards Rodriguez at the goal line, making him slightly more fantasy-valuable on a weekly basis barring big plays from Tuten. If this prediction comes true, both backs might have trouble cracking the weekly RB2 ranks.

Source: Sports Illustrated

item.title: Jeremiyah Love is behind Tyler Allgeier on Arizona’s unofficial depth chart for Week 1 at running back.
item.description:
Jeremiyah Love ARI Running Back

Seems unideal. The No. 3 overall pick in the draft is dealing with an ankle injury that may or may not have him in real trouble as far as playing in Week 1. Allgeier seems like he’ll at least have a real role in this backfield even if Love is healthy. This has not been a great early runout for those who picked Love early in fantasy drafts this offseason.

Source: Bo Brack

item.title: Chiefs coach Andy Reid said rookie UDFA Kahlil Benson would likely start at left tackle in Week 1.
item.description:
Kahlil Benson KC Tackle

Sure, that’s what Patrick Mahomes wants to see. Josh Simmons (back) is unlikely to play, leaving the Chiefs with Jaylon Moore at right tackle and Benson, who would become the first UDFA rookie to start at tackle in Week 1 since Desmond Harrison was with the Browns in 2018, on the blind side. “If he has to be the left tackle, then he’s the left tackle and we roll with it,” Reid said. “That’s just how it goes.” Inspiring stuff!

Source: The Athletic

item.title: Colts waived CB Jaylon Jones.
item.description:
Jaylon Jones

The 24-year-old former seventh-round pick — the other Jaylon Jones that plays cornerback — started 29 games in three years for the Colts. He’ll look for a fresh start after ending last year on injured reserve.

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Bears CB Kyler Gordon (calf) is working out on his own with a trainer to “accelerate his recovery.”
item.description:
Kyler Gordon CHI Defensive Back

Let’s hope he doesn’t find Joe Mixon’s trainers. Rapoport reports the “plan” is for Gordon to return a few weeks into the season and begin practicing shortly thereafter. He’s probably looking at a midseason timetable to return at this point.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: Jets coach Aaron Glenn said EDGE Joseph Ossai (foot) is week-to-week.
item.description:
Joseph Ossai NYJ Defensive End

He’s an IR possibility ahead of Week 1. Ossai, signed in the offseason from the Bengals, was expected to be a big part of the Jets rotation on the edge. His absence will elevate playing time for Will McDonald and Kingsley Enagbare.

Source: Eric Allen

item.title: Tyrone Tracy Jr., Najee Harris and Devin Singletary are all listed as co-No. 2 backs on New York’s unofficial Week 1 depth chart.
item.description:
Tyrone Tracy NYG Running Back

We can’t endorse relying on anyone in this backfield as a surefire bellcow in the event that Cam Skattebo gets hurt or is ineffective enough to lose playing time. It seems like it will be hard to rely on Tracy to have a major role this year with Harris in town.

Source: Jordan Raanan

item.title: Chiefs head coach Andy Reid said “there’s a good chance” Patrick Mahomes will start Week 1’s game against the Broncos.
item.description:
Patrick Mahomes KC Quarterback

We would be very surprised if Mahomes didn’t start Week 1 given how this has trended this offseason, but Reid left it in some doubt, adding “Most likely, he’ll be the guy that’s out there.” Justin Fields would be the starter if Mahomes couldn’t go, we doubt we’ll be talking about that possibility seriously on Friday or Saturday ahead of Kansas City’s MNF opener.

Source: Nate Taylor

item.title: Bears coach Ben Johnson said Rome Odunze (leg) is “day-to-day” and won’t practice Tuesday.
item.description:
Rome Odunze CHI Wide Receiver

Johnson added that he was “hopeful” Odunze would go on Sunday. Check back on Wednesday to see if he actually hits an injury report, but Odunze hasn’t practiced yet this week and that’s certainly not a great sign even if we’re not rushing to rule him out just yet.

Source: Kevin Fishbain

item.title: Chiefs coach Andy Reid said “there’s a good chance” Josh Simmons (back) won’t play this week.
item.description:
Josh Simmons KC Tackle

“He has a (back) issue there he’s working through. Josh is rehabbing. He’s working his tail off. This isn’t anything other than him having an issue with his back,” Reid said, asking what about his ‘My left tackle has a back issue he’s working through” t-shirt was unclear. Simmons’ status appears to be in some short-term doubt and we wouldn’t rule out an IR stint for him ahead of the opener.

Source: Sam McDowell

item.title: Eagles DE Brandon Graham retired after 16 NFL seasons.
item.description:
Brandon Graham

It’s a bit of a course reversal for the longtime Eagles pass rusher. Graham in May told reporters he would not retire and planned on suiting up for the 2026 season. On Tuesday he said he would hang it up after a fantastic career that included 79.5 sacks and two Super Bowl titles in Philadelphia. Graham, 38, who played all 16 years with the Eagles, had a career season in 2022 when he totaled 11 sacks to go along with 17 quarterback hits.

Source: Mike Garafolo

item.title: Bucs listed Jalen McMillan as a starting receiver on the team’s Week 1 depth chart.
item.description:
Jalen McMillan TB Wide Receiver

It’s McMillan, not rookie WR Ted Hurst III, who’s listed as a starter alongside Chris Godwin and Emeka Egbuka ahead of Tampa’s Week 1 game against the Bengals. Hurst, the tallest of the Bucs wideouts, has by all accounts impressed Bucs players and coaches throughout the offseason and should have some kind of role in the team’s passing attack to start the year. It could be a while before Hurst takes on a more prominent role, however. Bucs general manager Jason Licht said last week that Hurst, 22, has “proven to us throughout camp, even OTAs, practice every day that he’s been very, very steady...it’s kind of evolved into okay, we can use him this year and he’s going to play a role.” Hurst can be stashed in deeper fantasy formats for now. McMillan is unlikely to be a factor in the Tampa offense after once again struggling with injuries this offseason.

Source: Jenna Laine

item.title: The Chargers listed Charlie Kolar as the No. 1 tight end on their Week 1 depth chart.
item.description:
Charlie Kolar LAC Tight End

Way back in late May, the Athletic’s Daniel Popper suggested Kolar, who signed a three-year, $24.3 million contract with the Bolts this spring, would enter the season as LA’s top tight end “because of his complete skill set.” Week 1 usage will tell us a lot about how offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel will use his tight ends, but for now it seems Kolar will lead the group in Week 1 against the Cardinals. David Njoku and Oronde Gadsden II, however, could see more pass game involvement depending on how many routes they run in a given week, and whether the Chargers go run-heavy against an opponent. None of the Chargers’ tight ends are particularly appealing fantasy plays for Week 1.

Source: Chargers.com

item.title: The Athletic’s Joe Buscaglia believes Dalton Kincaid could become a “60 to 65 percent snap player” in 2026.
item.description:
Dalton Kincaid BUF Tight End

The most efficient tight end in the NFL over the past two seasons, Kincaid ran a pass route on a meager 45 percent of Buffalo’s drop backs over 12 games in 2025, finishing the season with 49 targets while being targeted on a hefty 28 percent of his routes. Finally healthy, Kincaid has been talked up by Bills coaches over the past few months. Bills players and beat writers have even complimented Kincaid’s blocking, a point of concern for the fourth-year tight end. Buscaglia said if Kincaid can “be just competent enough in blocking to preserve the threat of play action when he’s on the field and continue to crush receiving efficiency metrics, he’ll become one of the most important pieces to the roster.” Kincaid is a high upside swing late in drafts for those who fade the game’s top tight ends.

item.title: The Athletic’s Joe Buscaglia said he would not be surprised if DJ Moore is “on the field constantly and for [Josh] Allen to default to looking his way.”
item.description:
DJ Moore BUF Wide Receiver

Buscaglia called Moore, who was acquired from the Bears this spring, the “crown jewel of the offseason” for the Bills front office. “Moore’s contributions to the offense within training camp were immediate and obvious,” Buscaglia said. “Allen routinely pushed the ball downfield to Moore, making a concerted effort all summer to build on-field chemistry with the Bills’ new No. 1 receiver. ... The days of ‘everybody eats’ seem to be in the rearview mirror.” It’s a bullish report — one that could mean Moore is among the best values in redraft leagues this season even after being among the NFL’s most inefficient wideouts in 2025. Moore should be in all 12-team lineups for Week 1 against the Texans.

Source: The Athletic

item.title: ESPN’s Dan Graziano said it “sounds like” Malik Nabers (knee) will play in Week 1 against the Cowboys.
item.description:
Malik Nabers NYG Wide Receiver

Coming back from a 2025 ACL injury, there’s been speculation that Nabers might not be ready for the Giants’ opening game against Dallas on Sunday night. Graziano seems to think the Giants releasing veteran WR Darius Slayton over the weekend is a sign Nabers will be a go for Week 1, and ESPN’s Jordan Raanan said Nabers “seems to be trending in a positive direction” five days ahead of New York’s season opener. The Giants won’t practice Tuesday. Nabers’ Wednesday practice status could tell us whether he’s a full go against the Cowboys.

Source: Get Up ESPN

item.title: The Patriots and CB Christian Gonzalez are in agreement on a four-year, $135 million deal, according to ESPN’s Ian Rapoport.
item.description:
Christian Gonzalez NE Cornerback

It’s $102 million guaranteed for the 24-year-old Gonzalez, who is entering his fourth season after being drafted 17th overall in 2023. Gonzalez went without an interception during the regular season last year, but he was a Pro Bowler anyway and he did come up with a huge pick in the fourth quarter of the AFC Championship versus the Broncos. The Patriots had him under control for two more years after exercising his fifth-year option in April.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: 49ers OC Klay Kubiak said TE George Kittle “looks good” for Week 1.
item.description:
George Kittle SF Tight End

Asked whether Kittle would play in Week 1, 49ers offensive coordinator Klay Kubiak said, “We have two more practices, but Kittle looks good.” That was not as explicit as defensive coordinator Raheem Morris’ quote on Nick Bosa’s expected status just minutes earlier, but it certainly seems to confirm mounting reports that Kittle is on track to suit up for Week 1. Kubiak added at the end of his response that Kittle’s “workload will be determined,” also reinforcing earlier reports that the team was likely to monitor his snap rate closely. Fantasy managers are likely better off taking a wait-and-see approach with Kittle until he has proven to be capable of a normal workload.

item.title: 49ers DC Raheem Morris said DE Nick Bosa is going to play in Week 1 against the Rams.
item.description:
Nick Bosa SF Defensive Lineman

During a media sessions late Monday, Morris was asked if Bosa would be able to go in Week 1 against the Rams, to which he responded, “Oh, he’s going out there. He’s going.” There’s no room left for interpretation about that quote, meaning Bosa is expected to make his return to the field after tearing his ACL in Week 3 of the 2025 season. Don’t expect a normal allotment of snaps in his first game in almost a calendar year, but the veteran pass-rusher can still make a significant impact when on the field. IDP managers will want to confirm his status on the team’s injury report Tuesday before making plans to insert him into Week 1 lineups.

item.title: Seahawks WR Tory Horton (hamstring) was limited in practice Monday.
item.description:
Tory Horton SEA Wide Receiver

It was the second straight day with the same level of participation for the second-year receiver, who could be headed for a game-day injury designation for the team’s season opener. We were kept in the dark regarding Horton’s ailment after he missed the final three weeks of camp, with a hamstring injury now labeled as the cause. Although Jake Bobo’s season-ending ACL tear all but guaranteed Horton a spot on game-day rosters, he remains unlikely to contribute meaningful counting stats playing behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Rashid Shaheed, and Cooper Kupp. Second-year undrafted free agent Montorie Foster Jr would be in line to serve as the team’s fourth receiver on Wednesday should Horton be unable to go.

item.title: Seahawks S Ty Okada (hamstring) did not practice Sunday.
item.description:
Ty Okada SEA Free Safety

It’s the second straight missed practice for Okada as he tends to a hamstring injury, while fellow starting safety Nick Emmanwori (ankle) is thought to be doubtful to suit up against the Patriots Wednesday, per those close to the team. The team’s final injury report of their Week 1 preparation will be released Tuesday, upon which we’ll receive final game designations. Keep a close eye on the transaction reports from Seattle to gauge the expected level of health of both players. Considering the Seahawks carried only three safeties on their initial 53-man roster, any practice squad elevations from the secondary could signal expected absences from one, or both, players.

item.title: Seahawks HC Mike Macdonald said Zach Charbonnet (knee) is on target to meet his “aggressive” timetable for a return.
item.description:
Zach Charbonnet SEA Running Back

Macdonald wouldn’t reveal what the timetable was for Charbonnet’s return, but said the fourth-year back has looked “dang good” as he continues his rehab. Charbonnet will open this season on the PUP list, meaning he’ll be forced to miss at least the first four games of the season before the team can consider activating him to play. Charbonnet suffered a torn ACL in last year’s NFC Divisional Round game against the 49ers and is less than seven full months removed from the reconstruction surgery that took place on February 20th. The timing of his injury, coupled with the surgery, led many to believe Charbonnet would miss a significant portion of the season, but this talk of an “aggressive” timetable suggests he could be back far earlier than expected.

Source: Corbin Smith

item.title: Titans LB Cedric Gray is in concussion protocol.
item.description:
Cedric Gray TEN Linebacker

According to Titans beat Jim Wyatt, Gray was entered into concussion protocol after being involved in an accident while in an ultra terrain vehicle. The Titans released a statement saying that Gray “sustained a concussion and minor injuries” and that they expect him to be on the field once he clears concussion protocol. Gray is entering his third year in the league and is coming off a 2025 season in which he totaled 164 tackles, one sack, and two fumble recoveries while starting all 16 games he appeared in.

Source: Jim Wyatt

item.title: Giants released WR Darius Slayton.
item.description:
Darius Slayton

The longest-tenured Giants player is now in search of a new home after the team opted to release the 29-year-old receiver on Monday. Slayton was reportedly at risk of not making the initial 53-man roster out of camp, but survived the initial cuts only to be released a week later. During his seven seasons with the Giants, Slayton totaled 296 receptions for 4,435 yards and 22 touchdowns while serving primarily as a field stretcher. He posted four seasons of 724 or more receiving yards and had an impressive rookie campaign when he went for 48-740-8 as a rookie fifth-rounder out of Auburn. Slayton should have no trouble finding a new home in the coming days, but it may take some time before he’s back to seeing the field in a meaningful capacity.

Source: Matt Zenitz

item.title: Cardinals HC Mike LaFleur said he feels “good” about Jeremiyah Love’s (ankle) chances of playing in Week 1 against the Chargers.
item.description:
Jeremiyah Love ARI Running Back

LaFleur said Love is “progressing” well from the high ankle sprain he suffered this preseason and said the rookie running back “was out there moving around today.” It was reported last week by NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo that he had a 50/50 chance of playing in Week 1, but it sounds like he’s trending toward being ready for the season opener. The Cardinals will release their first official injury report on Wednesday, which should give us a better sense of Love’s availability before the weekend.

Source: Bo Brack

item.title: TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) did not practice on Monday.
item.description:
TreVeyon Henderson NE Running Back

Henderson traveled with the team to Seattle as it prepares for Wednesday’s game against the Seahawks, but he was unable to get on the practice field. That’s now back-to-back DNPs for Henderson, who is trending toward missing the season opener. Unless he can log a limited practice on Tuesday, it wouldn’t be surprising if Henderson was ruled out well before Wednesday’s game, paving the way for Rhamondre Stevenson to have a busy Week 1 in this rematch between last year’s Super Bowl contenders.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: Chargers RB Keaton Mitchell was seen practicing on Monday.
item.description:
Keaton Mitchell LAC Running Back

Mitchell missed the last six practices due to an undisclosed injury but was on the field Monday participating in drills. The Chargers don’t need to disclose any specifics regarding Mitchell’s injury until Wednesday, when they release their first official injury report of the season, but his return on Monday is an encouraging sign. Mitchell is expected to work into the mix with Omarion Hampton, who will serve as the unquestioned RB1 for the Chargers this season. Whether or not Mitchell sees enough work to be fantasy viable is to be determined, but there’s some belief he could see some work in the passing game, which could establish a decent floor for him in half and full-PPR leagues. Mitchell is an intriguing stash in fantasy leagues, but managers shouldn’t be rushing to put him in their starting lineups just yet.

Source: Kris Rhim

item.title: Speaking on the Pat McAfee Show, ESPN’s Adam Schefter said “I think there’s a real possibility” that Puka Nacua avoids any discipline this season.
item.description:
Puka Nacua

This, of course, is in reference to the civil lawsuit that was filed against Nacua that alleges he bit a woman and made an “unprovoked antisemitic sentiment.” The Rams receiver avoided being placed on the commissioner’s exempt list and will travel with the team to Australia to play in their season opener against the 49ers. Nacua has been dealing with a psoas injury since August, but head coach Sean McVay said they expect him to play in Week 1. Nacua profiles as a high-end WR1 against a familiar foe in the Niners.

Source: Pat McAfee

item.title: Steelers HC Mike McCarthy said he expects Joey Porter Jr. to play in Week 1 against the Falcons.
item.description:
Joey Porter PIT Cornerback

Porter has been seeking a new contract from the Steelers all offseason, but all reports indicate the two sides are far apart on a deal. While Porter has been noncommittal about playing without a new contract, he was seen on the field during Monday’s practice and was activated from the PUP list last week. These encouraging signs, coupled with McCarthy’s confidence in him playing, are more than enough to suggest Porter will be on the field for the season opener on Sunday against the Falcons. Porter totaled 52 tackles, 14 pass breakups, and one interception last season while earning a PFF coverage grade of 74.1. Update: Steelers beat writer Nick Farbaugh later noted that McCarthy said the team will “see what happens” if Porter doesn’t play, while also adding that there are “definitely still business conversations” going on regarding an extension.

Source: Nick Farabaugh

item.title: Colts HC Shane Steichen said Alec Pierce (ankle) is expected to play in Week 1 against the Ravens.
item.description:
Alec Pierce IND Wide Receiver

Pierce missed most of training camp while recovering from offseason ankle surgery, but the fifth-year speedster is expected to be on the field when the Colts take on the Ravens in the season opener. ESPN’s Stephen Holder noted that “it’s very possible” some of Pierce’s workload will be split between Keenan Allen and Ashton Dulin as he continues to ramp up after an extended absence, but Pierce will be on the field in some capacity on Sunday. Unfortunately, this makes him a risky bet for fantasy purposes unless Steichen can alleviate any concerns about Pierce being on a pitch count to start the season.

Source: Stephen Holder

item.title: Cowboys HC Brian Schottenheimer said LG Tyler Smith will undergo thumb surgery and be sidelined for four to six weeks.
item.description:
Tyler Smith DAL Guard

The All-Pro guard started all 16 games he appeared in last season and has been named to the Pro Bowl each of the last three seasons. According to ESPN’s Todd Archer, Smith “

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: Texans HC DeMeco Ryans said Kayshon Boutte will play in Week 1 against the Bills.
item.description:
Kayshon Boutte HOU Wide Receiver

Speaking on Monday, Ryans said Boutte has been “picking up the playbook really well.” The fourth-year receiver was acquired in a trade with the Patriots back on August 24th and is expected to have an immediate role in the offense after the Texans lost Jayden Higgins to a torn ACL earlier this offseason. Boutte has served primarily as a field stretcher during his first three years in the league and shouldn’t be trusted in start/sit leagues this week.

Source: DJ Bien-Aime

item.title: Isiah Bond (concussion) was seen practicing on Monday.
item.description:
Isaiah Bond CLE Wide Receiver

Bond suffered a concussion last week and has been sidelined ever since. On Monday, however, the second-year receiver was spotted at practice and participating in team drills. Bond is currently stuck behind Jerry Jeudy, KC Concepcion, and Denzel Boston on the depth chart after totaling 18 receptions for 338 scoreless yards as a rookie last season. He doesn’t have any fantasy value at this time.

Source: Mary Kay Cabot

item.title: Rome Odunze (leg) was not seen practicing on Monday.
item.description:
Rome Odunze CHI Wide Receiver

Odunze suffered a leg injury on Thursday. The Athletic’s Dan Wiederer said later in the day that the belief is that Odunze “should be all good” after the injury scare, but it’s something to keep an eye on this week. The Bears won’t release their first injury report until Wednesday, which could serve as the first clear look at where things stand for Odunze for Week 1 against the Panthers. If he is unable to go, second-year players Luther Burden and Colston Loveland could both see a slight uptick in target volume.

Source: Courtney Cronin

item.title: Kyle Monangai (knee) returned to practice on Monday.
item.description:
Kyle Monangai CHI Running Back

After missing a few weeks of practice with a hyperextended knee he suffered in camp, Monangai was back at practice on Monday to begin prepping for Week 1’s game against the Panthers. Monangai’s status will be worth checking when the Bears release their first injury report on Wednesday, but it sounds like he’ll have a chance to play this week barring any setbacks. In addition to Monangai, D’Andre Swift, who left last Thursday’s practice with cramps, also returned to the field.

Source: Courtney Cronin

item.title: Buccaneers HC Todd Bowles said RB Sean Tucker (undisclosed) will be a game-time decision for Week 1 against the Bengals.
item.description:
Sean Tucker TB Running Back

Bowles didn’t disclose what Tucker is dealing with because he doesn’t have to do that until Wednesday, when the team releases its first injury report. That said, it sounds like Tucker is facing an uphill battle to be ready for Week 1, and we know he was sidelined for Monday’s practice. His absence isn’t expected to have much of a fantasy impact, as Tucker is expected to serve as the third RB for the Bucs behind both Bucky Irving and Kenneth Gainwell.

Source: Greg Auman

item.title: Browns HC Todd Monken said it’s possible QB Taylen Green will be active for Week 1 against the Jaguars.
item.description:
Taylen Green CLE Quarterback

When speaking with the media on Monday, Monken said, “There could be a package where we have (Green)” on the field. Monken also suggested he

Source: Mary Kay Cabot

item.title: Ja’Marr Chase (knee) was seen practicing on Monday.
item.description:
Ja'Marr Chase CIN Wide Receiver

Tee Higgins (heel contusion) was also spotted at practice after both players were said to be limited participants last week. The Bengals won’t release their first official injury report of the week until Wednesday, but it doesn’t sound like either Chase or Higgins is at risk of missing Week 1’s game against the Buccaneers. As usual, Chase profiles as a high-end fantasy WR1, while Higgins should be viewed more as a WR2 with WR1 upside in any given week.

Source: Kelsey Conway

item.title: Browns HC Todd Monken said Maliek Collins is “good to go” ahead of Week 1’s game against the Jaguars.
item.description:
Maliek Collins CLE Defensive Tackle

Collins opened training camp on the PUP list due to a quad injury that ended his 2025 campaign. He was activated from the PUP list two weeks ago and has been practicing with the team and appears to be in position to play in Week 1 against the Jags. Collins totaled 25 tackles, seven TFLs, and 6.5 sacks in the 12 games he appeared in last season for the Browns and has tallied five or more sacks in each of his last three seasons.

Source: Daniel Oyefusi

item.title: Lions HC Dan Campbell said Jacob Saylors and Sione Vaki could both push for RB2 touches behind Jahmyr Gibbs.
item.description:
Jacob Saylors DET Running Back

It’s hard to imagine either Vaki or Saylors having meaningful fantasy value at this point in the season, but it sounds like both will be on the field while Isiah Pacheco (back) is sidelined for at least the first four games of the season. Judging by how Campbell sounded when discussing each player, it sounded like Saylors might be closer to the official RB2, but Campbell didn’t mince words when he said, “I see Vaki getting some reps, too.” Fantasy managers interested in taking a shot on a Lions running back not named Jahmyr Gibbs can consider both Saylors and Vaki as late-round dart throws until we see how their snap shares look in the coming weeks.

Source: Detroit Lions

item.title: Emeka Egbuka (toe) practiced on Monday.
item.description:
Emeka Egbuka TB Wide Receiver

Egbuka was working with trainers last week, but was on the field with the team on Monday. The Buccaneers won’t release their first official injury report until Wednesday, but it sounds like Egbuka is trending in the right direction ahead of the Buccaneers’ Week 1 game against the Bengals. Egbuka has been dealing with this toe injury since mid-August, but it seems like the Bucs have slowly ramped him up as of late. His practice status will be one to monitor when the first injury report drops. In addition to Egbuka, WR Jalen McMillan and OT Justin Skule were also practicing, while RB Sean Tucker was not seen on the field.

Source: Rick Stroud

item.title: Panthers TE Darren Waller practiced on Monday.
item.description:
Darren Waller CAR Tight End

Waller looked “big and fast” in Monday practice, per head coach Dave Canales, and reportedly hit 20 MPH on one of his routes. The veteran tight end was seen catching passes from Bryce Young and could have a chance to suit up for the Panthers’ Week 1 game against the Bears. It’s still too early to know how significant a role Waller will have in Canales’ offense, but he could have some fantasy viability as a streaming option in what is a very thin tight end room in Carolina.

Source: Mike Kaye

item.title: Broncos signed S Taylor Rapp.
item.description:
Taylor Rapp DEN Safety

Rapp will start the season on the Broncos’ practice squad after being released by the team last week. With 72 career starts under his belt, Rapp should have a chance to work his way onto the Broncos’ 53-man roster at some point this season and could serve as valuable depth for one of the league’s best defenses. Rapp totaled 26 tackles in six games for the Bills last season before a knee injury prematurely ended his season.

item.title: Commanders signed WR Van Jefferson.
item.description:
Van Jefferson WAS Wide Receiver

Jefferson spent all offseason with the Commanders but found himself on the outside looking in when camp cuts came around. The 30-year-old receiver caught 29 passes for 350 yards and one touchdown last season with the Titans and has bounced around the league over the last four seasons. He could be an injury away from being promoted to the 53-man roster, but we wouldn’t expect him to offer much fantasy production even if he is active on game day.

Source: Nicki Jhabvala

item.title: Jonathon Brooks (soreness) was seen working off to the side with trainers on Monday.
item.description:
Jonathon Brooks CAR Running Back

Head coach Dave Canales declined to provide an update on Brooks’ status Monday after saying last week that he was “very optimistic” that Brooks would play in Week 1 against the Bears. The Panthers won’t release their first official injury report until Wednesday, which should give us a better idea of where things stand for Brooks in the season opener. The 23-year-old back has had a strong training camp and is expected to split work with Chuba Hubbard if active. Both RBs should be viewed in the RB3 range for Week 1 if active.

Source: Joe Person

item.title: Patriots HC Mike Vrabel said “we’ll see how he feels today” when asked about the status of TreVeyon Henderson (ankle).
item.description:
TreVeyon Henderson NE Running Back

Henderson has missed multiple weeks of practice since sustaining an ankle injury on August 24. After being a DNP on Sunday, Henderson missing Monday’s practice would be a bad sign for his availability for Wednesday’s season opener against the Seahawks. The Patriots will take the field later in the day, so we should have an update soon on whether or not he’s with the team. If he’s unable to play on Wednesday, Rhamondre Stevenson would be in line to handle a significant workload against a stout Seahawks defense.

Source: Mike Reiss

item.title: Falcons HC Kevin Stefanski said Michael Penix will be inactive for Week 1 against the Steelers.
item.description:
Michael Penix ATL Quarterback

Veteran QB Cooper Rush will serve as the Falcons’ QB2 in the season opener. Speaking on Monday with the media, Stefanski declined to put a timeline on when Penix could be ready to take the field, instead saying he is “very confident in the plan” they have for the 26-year-old QB. Earlier, NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reported that the Falcons wanted to give Penix “a couple more weeks” to prepare for the season, so it wouldn’t be surprising if we are a few weeks away from him dressing for game days.

Source: D. Orlando Ledbetter

item.title: 49ers WR Mike Evans said the injuries he was dealing with in training camp were not “significant.”
item.description:
Mike Evans SF Wide Receiver

This is an encouraging piece of news from Evans, who dealt with a quad injury and an abductor injury during training camp. According to the 33-year-old vet, none of the injuries he was dealing with would have resulted in him missing game time, which should give fantasy managers a boost of confidence entering this season. Evans signed a three-year contract with the 49ers this offseason and is coming off a year in which he was limited to just eight games due to a hamstring injury and a broken clavicle. Evans is expected to serve as the Niners’ WR1 this season and profiles as a high-upside WR2 in fantasy who should provide plenty of big weeks this season.

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Michael Penix “did not believe that he was ready” to play in Week 1 against the Steelers.
item.description:
Michael Penix ATL Quarterback

Penix was cleared to participate in 11-on-11s back on August 22 and hasn’t logged much practice in camp. As a result, Tua Tagovailoa has been named the starter for the Falcons to kick off Week 1 against the Steelers, buying Penix some additional time to get practice reps and get his knee right before being put in game situations. Rapoport said the Falcons hope to give Penix “a couple more weeks” before playing him, so it wouldn’t be surprising if we saw Tua under center for the first few games of the season before the Falcons consider a switch at the position. Tagovailoa struggled in camp and throughout the preseason and is expected to be on a short leash once Penix is ready to go.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: George Kittle (Achilles) was seen practicing on Monday.
item.description:
George Kittle SF Tight End

Kittle was on the field on Monday when the Niners took the field to begin prepping for their Week 1 opener against the Rams in Australia. The veteran tight end has long been expected to have a shot to play in Thursday’s game, so the fact that he was on the field doesn’t come as much of a surprise. Kittle was able to log a few practices last week, but could be on a bit of a pitch count in his first game since suffering a torn Achilles in mid-January. Assuming he is limited in some capacity, Kittle should be viewed as a boom/bust TE1 for fantasy purposes.

Source: Matt Maiocco

item.title: Christian McCaffrey was not spotted at the early portion of Monday’s practice.
item.description:
Christian McCaffrey SF Running Back

While most of us were asleep on Sunday night, the 49ers were already conducting a Monday afternoon practice in Australia. According to NBC Sports’ Matt Maiocco, McCaffrey was not seen taking part in drills during the early portion of practice. It’s possible this is by design as the Niners prepare for their season opener on Thursday against the Rams, so we won’t read too much into this just yet. McCaffrey missed some time during training camp due to “tightness,” but seemingly downplayed any idea of an injury when he later said the time off during camp was “the plan from the jump.” This is something to keep an eye on in the coming days, but for now, we’ll assume McCaffrey will be good to go for the season opener. According to Maiocco, DE Nick Bosa was also not spotted during the early portion of practice on Monday.

Source: Matt Maiocco

item.title: Falcons announced Tua Tagovailoa will start in Week 1 against the Steelers.
item.description:
Tua Tagovailoa ATL Quarterback

Despite an up-and-down training camp, Tagovailoa will get the nod as the starter when the Falcons kick off the season on Sunday against the Steelers. Given the fact that Michael Penix Jr. (knee) was still limited at the start of camp, Tagovailoa had long been assumed to have the inside edge on the QB1 job at the start of camp, but Penix was still given a shot to compete for the job despite not being cleared for 11-on-11 practice until August 22. Tagovailoa shouldn’t be counted on in standard 1QB leagues at this point, and fantasy managers looking to add him in 2QB and superflex leagues shouldn’t view him as a long-term solution. It would not be at all surprising if we saw both Tagovailoa and Penix start multiple games for the Falcons this season, with rookie UDFA Jack Stand also being a dark horse to see snaps at some point in the season after an impressive training camp and preseason.

Source: Tom Pelissero

item.title: The Athletic’s Daniel Popper believes that Chargers RB Keaton Mitchell “is going to do a lot of nice things in the offense.”
item.description:
Keaton Mitchell LAC Running Back

Popper makes clear that RB Omarion Hampton will be an offensive centerpiece, but Mitchell should have his own helpful role as well. Mitchell will be involved in the passing game, at times lining up outside and getting involved “vertically” as a receiver. Mitchell will need to maximize his touches if he is going to warrant FLEX treatment as Hampton’s sidekick, and his health remains a question at the moment, as he deals with an undisclosed injury. On the plus side, Popper did not mention the ailment at all, which could be taken as a positive.

Source: Locked On Chargers

item.title: The Athletic’s Daniel Popper said a top-five season for Chargers RB Omarion Hampton is “realistic.”
item.description:
Omarion Hampton LAC Running Back

Popper fielded a question about Hampton’s top-10 chances as a guest on the Locked On Chargers show. The metrics for measuring this feat were left undefined, but rushing yardage or scrimmage yardage are the two most likely baselines. While OC Mike McDaniel has teased a potential hot-hand approach, Popper has remained steadfast in his stance that Hampton is set for bellcow duties thanks in part to speed, physicality and scheme versatility. He warrants RB1 treatment right out of the gate.

Source: Locked On Chargers

item.title: The Athletic’s Daniel Popper thinks Chargers EDGE Tuli Tuipulotu will play out the final year of his contract this season.
item.description:
Tuli Tuipulotu LAC Outside Linebacker

Tuipulotu, 24, led the Chargers with 70 quarterback pressures and 13 sacks last season. He is scheduled to enter free agency next offseason. According to Popper, the team would like to see Tuipulotu “do it again” before paying him like a top pass rusher. Tuipulotu has already proven himself. He totaled 40 quarterback pressures and nine sacks in 2024 and 51 quarterback pressures and eight sacks as a 2023 rookie. An in-season extension is possible.

Source: Locked On Chargers

item.title: Patriots RB TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) did not practice on Sunday.
item.description:
TreVeyon Henderson NE Running Back

This outcome is unsurprising, given his absence during the portion of practice open to the media. If Henderson is unable to play on Wednesday night, starting RB Rhamondre Stevenson would take on a sizable workload. Backup RB Corey Kiner and practice squad players RB Lan Larison and RB Hassan Haskins are the Patriots’ remaining backfield members.

Source: Mike Reiss

item.title: Patriots DT Christian Barmore (knee) did not practice on Sunday.
item.description:
Christian Barmore NE Defensive Tackle

Barmore is a pivotal player in the Patriots’ defensive front. He racked up 20 tackles, 50 quarterback pressures and two sacks last season. If he is unable to face the Seahawks this week, his absence would be consequential.

Source: Mike Reiss

item.title: Seahawks RB Emanuel Wilson (hamstring) is practicing in full for Week 1 against the Patriots.
item.description:
Emanuel Wilson SEA Running Back

Wilson is the wildcard in the Seahawks’ backfield. If he logs 6-8 touches, he can reduce RB Jadarian Price’s and RB George Holani’s fantasy-scoring outlook. That said, he is third on the depth chart for a reason and can only be viewed as a mildly interesting bench stash in very deep leagues.

Source: Seattle Seahawks

item.title: Seahawks WR Tory Horton (hamstring) was limited on Sunday.
item.description:
Tory Horton SEA Wide Receiver

Now we know what has kept Horton sidelined since mid-August. Although the speedy wide receiver has resumed practicing, which is a good sign, he is not guaranteed to suit up. If active, he is likely only relevant in single-game DFS contests.

Source: Brady Henderson

item.title: Seahawks TE AJ Barner (oblique) is practicing in full for Week 1 against the Patriots.
item.description:
AJ Barner SEA Tight End

The Seahawks’ starting tight end is firmly on track to play in the 2026 season opener on Wednesday night. Barner is reportedly set to handle a bigger role than he did last year, when he finished as the PPR TE14. He can only be viewed as a borderline TE1/2 early on, though.

Source: Brady Henderson

item.title: Rams coach Sean McVay said the expectation is that WR Puka Nacua (psoas) will play in Week 1 against the 49ers.
item.description:
Puka Nacua

McVay’s comments also relate to Nacua’s status with the league office. The 25-year-old wide receiver was at one point thought to be a suspension candidate, but the league has made no such ruling while doling out suspensions and Commissioner Exempt List placements elsewhere in the league. Rams LT Alaric Jackson was also a suspension candidate, but is expected to play in Week 1, per McVay. His presence positively impacts the Rams’ passing game outlook. Assuming he is active, Nacua can be treated as an elite WR1.

Source: Nate Atkins

item.title: Giants signed OG Jon Runyan to a two-year, $22 million extension through 2028.
item.description:
Jon Runyan NYG Guard

According to ESPN’s Adam Schefter, the deal includes $21.5 million in guarantees. He was entering the final year of a three-year, $30 million contract signed in the 2024 offseason. The 29-year-old is probably more of a stopgap than a long-term fixture for the Giants at this point, but he should start in Week 1.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: ESPN’s Brady Henderson believes Seahawks LB Ernest Jones’ comments “seemed to convey doubt that” S Nick Emmanwori (ankle) will play in Week 1 against the Patriots.
item.description:
Nick Emmanwori SEA Safety

Henderson’s assessment is reasonable. Jones’ comments on Emmanwori’s abilities meandered, but he closed by saying the team is “focused on who’s out there, who’s available right now.” Emmanwori underwent surgery to deal with a nagging ankle issue in July. Seahawks GM John Schneider said recent trade acquisition CB Avery Smith had a “phenomenal preseason” and can line up on the perimeter and over the slot, making him a potential fill-in for Emmanwori’s hybrid nickel/safety role.

Source: Brady Henderson

item.title: Sports Illustrated’s John Shipley reports that Travis Hunter “is expected to be the Jaguars’ No. 1 cornerback in Week 1 and beyond.”
item.description:
Travis Hunter

Shipley leaves the light on for offensive contributions, entertaining the idea that Hunter can chip in “a few hundred yards and a few touchdowns” this season as well. That said, the early indications for Hunter’s FLEX viability in managed leagues are pretty bleak. Stash him if you wish, but understand that starting him in Week 1 against the Browns could result in zero points.

Source: Sports Illustrated

item.title: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that Seahawks RB Jadarian Price “is going to be a big factor,” but the team will use “two or three” running backs this year.
item.description:
Jadarian Price SEA Running Back

This report largely affirms what we already believed to be true. Price can be expected to lead the backfield in carries, although Fowler thinks his workload will fall short of 20 carries per game. Few running backs hit that mark anyway, so that is hardly surprising. A report from The Athletic suggested RB George Holani could be trusted to handle high-value touches on passing downs and is scoring position, which hurts Price’s outlook. If only two running backs are involved, though, Price should provide usable stat lines. If Emanuel Wilson gets involved this could become a fantasy-unfriendly situation.

Source: Jeremy Fowler

item.title: The Athletic’s Nate Atkins reports that Rams EDGE Myles Garrett (knee) and DT Aaron Donald will practice today.
item.description:
Myles Garrett

Garrett, 30, has been sidelined by swelling in his knee since late July. His return to practice puts him on track to play in Week 1 against the 49ers on Thursday. Donald’s status is tougher to decipher. The fact that he is practicing is a great sign, but the Rams could still slow-play his return to action. Rams coach Sean McVay said he will provide an update on their Week 1 statuses on Tuesday. Stay tuned.

Source: Nate Atkins

item.title: Giants signed QB Jameis Winston to a two-year, $13 million extension through 2028.
item.description:
Jameis Winston NYG Quarterback

Winston, 32, will remain in New York as QB Jaxson Dart’s mentor for the foreseeable future. He is a capable, fantasy-friendly backup who can bridge the gap if Dart misses time. Winston started two games last year, completing 37-of-65 passes for 567 yards, two touchdowns and two interceptions, and rushing seven times for 23 yards and one touchdown while fumbling once.

Source: Jordan Schultz

item.title: ESPN’s Mike Reiss reports that Patriots RB Rhamondre Stevenson is “the clear-cut starter.”
item.description:
Rhamondre Stevenson NE Running Back

Stevenson’s position on the depth chart has been apparent for some time, but Reiss helpfully states it in plain terms after rhetorically asking how the Patriots will handle in-game running back reps if RB TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) cannot play in Week 1 against the Seahawks on Wednesday night. If Henderson is unable to play, Stevenson will likely take on a larger-than-normal workload, with RB Corey Kiner and practice squad members RB Lan Larison and/or RB Hassan Haskins serving as his in-house touch competition. Although the Seahawks field a top-tier run defense, Stevenson can be treated as a high-end RB2 if Henderson is out, thanks to his hefty workload.

Source: ESPN
